On 2026-08-13 the user confirmed that the failure occurs when one provider host launches another provider through CLI mode, such as Claude invoking Codex or Codex invoking Claude. A ten-minute caller timeout can detach or terminate observation even though the provider process may still be doing useful work. The related B-1be5 proposal only considered heuristic ledger provenance and does not solve this execution failure. During B-137a PLAN scope review, the first design was formally reopened because its evidence write ordering would either deadlock before terminal or let the controller impersonate the reviewer.

## Key Insights

The framework must supervise the provider process at the actual execution boundary. A worker heartbeat and provider progress are different facts; output silence is diagnostic rather than terminal. Every wait must be bounded, every run must have a finite absolute deadline, and a durable next-touch reconciler must be able to materialize terminal truth even when the original worker becomes wedged. Formal reviewer evidence must bind to the exact managed receipt instead of provider plus story plus time-window guesses.

Reviewer evidence also needs a two-phase provenance protocol. The provider reviewer authors an immutable proposal containing its pass/findings and truthful read evidence while the run is active. It cannot call the final evidence writer before the terminal receipt and evidence journal are sealed. After successful terminal, a mechanical importer validates the sealed proposal and imports it without allowing the controller to change the verdict or become the reviewer. The new composite evidence class must use the existing shared Proof Admissibility artifact registry, intake, reason vocabulary and evaluator at both write-time and REVIEW-gate consumption; a parallel special-case proof system is not acceptable.

## Solution Tradeoffs

A single deep ManagedHostRun module adds durable runtime artifacts, worker continuation and reconciliation complexity, but removes duplicated foreground/background supervision and makes cancellation, cleanup and evidence semantics consistent. M1 execution safety and M2 gate evidence ship together so the framework does not claim enforcement while raw CLI reviews can still satisfy formal gates. The two-phase proposal/import protocol adds one post-terminal mechanical step, but preserves the actual provider reviewer as evidence author and prevents controller self-absolution. Reusing shared Proof Admissibility adds registry work but avoids a second trust vocabulary and keeps gate-consumed facts centrally auditable. Legacy configured provider timeout ceilings remain separate and unchanged.

## Conversational Texture

The user repeatedly emphasized that a ten-minute boundary must not cause an automatic restart, that silent but still-running agents should continue to be monitored, and that the target is host-independent cross-provider CLI execution rather than native subagent APIs. After iterative Claude Opus review and empirical Codex/POSIX probes, the user approved the consolidated design and explicitly asked to start a Story and implement it. The behavior-facing seams are:
1. `host_run` submit/foreground attach;
2. `host_run_status(runId, waitMs<=30000)`;
3. `host_run_cancel(runId, reason?)`;
4. `cross_host_review` as the privileged verdict-profile owner;
5. `review_pass_set` / `finding_add` plus the REVIEW gate as managed-evidence consumers.

Private worker, file layout, launch adapters and reconciliation helpers are tested only through those seams or through real child-process effects. Each vertical slice follows RED → minimal GREEN; implementation does not bulk-create imagined internal tests.

## CHK-001 — Persist and reconcile managed host-run lifecycle

Create a deep `core/managed-host-run.ts` module whose small interface owns submit, attach/status projection, cancel, worker execution and reconcile. A run gets a generated `hrun_*` identity and an immutable root under `.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`.

Submit writes immutable/spec-bound state atomically: `spec.json`, digest-only `owner.json`, 0600 one-shot `input.cap` and `input.prompt`, initial `snapshot.json`, and append-only `events.jsonl`. The hidden worker wins `claim.json` using exclusive create, validates the one-shot capability, unlinks both input files, marks `claimReady`, acquires provider admission, launches the private provider adapter and periodically advances `workerHeartbeatAt`. Provider output updates a separate `lastProviderProgressAt` only when observable; unsupported observability is represented as `unobservable`, never fabricated.

A terminal is created exclusively and exactly once. It records outcome, timing, exit/timeout/cancel reason, provider identity, spec/profile binding digests, evidence journal digest, process cleanup facts, residual process state and an independent `replacementSafe`. Repeated status/cancel/attach calls first acquire a short `reconcile.lock`, re-read facts, and materialize terminal truth for deadline expiry or authoritative worker/provider death. Silence is never a transition predicate. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity yields honest residual `unknown` and `replacementSafe:false`, not blind termination.

+# Managed cross-provider CLI execution
+
+Status: Adopted
+Story: B-137a
+Date: 2026-08-14
+
+## Context
+
+When a Claude host started Codex (or a Codex host started Claude) with raw shell
+execution, the caller owned the child process implicitly. A caller watchdog,
+terminal disconnect, or ten-minute foreground boundary could end observation
+without proving that the provider had failed. Treating that loss of observation
+as failure caused duplicate reviewer launches; treating `running` forever as
+proof of health caused unbounded waits. Output silence alone answers neither
+question.
+
+Proofbound is host-neutral. Native Codex/Claude subagent lifecycle APIs are not
+portable and therefore are not the execution contract. This decision covers
+only Proofbound-owned cross-provider CLI processes.
+
+## Decision
+
+Proofbound owns every public `host_run` and every formal cross-provider CLI
+reviewer launch through a durable `ManagedHostRun`. General provider workloads
+such as planned steps and autopilot repair keep their existing bounded adapters
+but share the mandatory provider-process admission registry; they do not claim
+durable reviewer ownership or reviewer evidence. The caller submits and
+observes; a detached worker owns the managed provider process until an exclusive
+terminal record exists.
+
+The public surface is:
+
+- `host_run`: submit, optionally attach in foreground, or return after claim
+  with `--detach`;
+- `host_run_status`: read or long-poll one run for at most 30 seconds;
+- `host_run_cancel`: idempotently request cancellation;
+- `host_run_worker`: private runtime continuation, dispatchable internally but
+  hidden from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
+- `managed_review_proposal_set`: compatibility-only provider callback for older
+  adapters, not the formal managed happy path;
+- `managed_review_evidence_import`: verdict-free exact-receipt importer.
+
+`cross_host_review` remains the policy/profile owner for paired host verdicts,
+but its Codex leaf executes inside ManagedHostRun and exposes the managed run
+and receipt in host-B provenance.
+
+## State and liveness contract
+
+The states are `submitted`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and
+`timed_out`. Exactly one terminal file wins by exclusive creation. Repeated
+status, cancel and resume operations are idempotent and never create a new run.
+
+Two clocks are deliberately distinct:
+
+- `workerHeartbeatAt` shows that the supervisor can still update its durable
+  snapshot;
+- `lastProviderProgressAt` changes only when observable provider stdout/stderr
+  arrives.
+
+Neither clock is a completion oracle. A provider may legitimately be silent,
+and a worker heartbeat does not prove provider progress. Expiry of a 30-second
+observation wait is non-terminal: it only wakes the caller and never authorizes
+a retry. The `host_run_status` call is also the run's next-touch reconciler,
+however, so during that call an already-requested cancellation or an expired
+absolute deadline can legitimately publish the corresponding `cancelled` or
+`timed_out` terminal state.
+
+Every run has a finite absolute deadline (30 minutes by default, bounded to 24
+hours). Deadline or cancellation reconciliation performs bounded TERM, KILL,
+reap and residual probing. Replacement is safe only when cleanup facts prove
+there is no residual process group. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity remains
+`replacementSafe=false`; it is not guessed away.
+
+## Persistence and process ownership
+
+Each run has a 0700 directory at
+`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
+primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
+DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
+bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
+capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
+Prompt, capability and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot inputs;
+the worker validates and deletes them before provider launch. Only root and
+runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.
+
+On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Codex receives the
+prompt through documented stdin (`codex exec ... -`) and Claude receives a 0600
+one-shot prompt file. The current agy print launcher accepts prompt text only in
+argv, so managed agy execution refuses before provider spawn until agy exposes a
+stdin or protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms likewise refuse
+before provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup is equivalent.
+
+## Shared provider admission
+
+Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
+of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
+token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
+Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
+not process admission.
+
+A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
+reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
+checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
+already been reclaimed and reassigned.
+
+Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
+admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
+review evidence.
+
+## Formal managed reviewer evidence
+
+Native-host reviewers retain the existing signed ReviewRun plus direct
+ReviewPass/Finding flow. A cross-provider CLI reviewer uses a two-phase flow:
+
+1. The controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
+2. `host_run --managedReview` derives the exact assembled prompt and seals
+   story, provider, lane, ReviewRun, head, material, story-files and prompt
+   bindings.
+3. The managed prompt requires the provider's final assistant result to be one
+   bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope with
+   pass-or-findings and truthful read evidence. It cannot write final
+   `review_pass_set`/`finding_add` evidence from inside the managed run. After a
+   successful provider exit, the owning adapter selects only Codex's terminal
+   `item.completed` `agent_message` or Claude's terminal `result`; tool logs,
+   arbitrary stdout and controller fields are never proposal inputs. The worker
+   validates the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple and atomically writes
+   the immutable proposal. Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized final
+   envelopes fail the managed run closed. The older descriptor-authorized
+   `managed_review_proposal_set` callback remains compatibility-only.
+4. Successful terminal creation seals spec, proposal, result and event-journal
+   digests plus cleanup facts.
+5. The controller calls `managed_review_evidence_import` with only the exact
+   runId and receiptId. It cannot provide or alter verdict bytes.
+6. The importer preserves provider reviewer/lane/ReviewRun/read provenance and
+   writes the existing signed ReviewPass/Finding shape.
+7. Import time and the REVIEW gate both call the shared Proof Admissibility
+   registry/intake/evaluator and revalidate the current terminal, proposal,
+   journal, prompt and material tuple.
+
+Raw CLI output outside the trusted final-result adapter lane, usage-ledger rows, time-window correlations, pre-terminal
+proposals, failed/cancelled/timed-out terminals and controller-authored verdicts
+cannot upgrade to managed reviewer evidence. Raw same-UID CLI calls, forged
+environment values, stale process groups, terminal/reaped runs and
+ambiguous/multiple active candidates cannot borrow the descriptor authority.
+
+The authority classifications remain disjoint. A native-host reviewer keeps the
+signed ReviewRun plus direct ReviewPass/Finding path only when a registered
+host-adapter broker signs the exact closeout invocation. Its Ed25519 attestation
+binds Story, agent/lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch,
+adapter/host identity and a one-shot nonce. Lattice stores the registered public
+key and nonce-consumption record, but exposes no issuer command and stores no
+broker private key. `dispatch`, `review_run_start`, inherited environment values
+and raw provider CLIs cannot mint this authority. The host adapter must inject
+the signed attestation over a dedicated descriptor for the exact CLI process;
+without that integration, native direct evidence is advisory-only and formal
+review must use the managed path.
+
+Process ancestry is secondary evidence. An unobservable process table, as in a
+brokered desktop sandbox, does not negate a valid broker signature. When a full
+ancestry is observable, any mixed distinct provider families (Claude→Codex or
+Codex→Claude) veto direct evidence even if the nearest ancestor matches. The
+one-shot local nonce ledger prevents replay but is not represented as protection
+against a same-UID/root attacker capable of replacing trusted configuration or
+instrumenting the broker.
+
+A cross-provider CLI reviewer requires a managed terminal receipt;
+cross-provider CLI output without that receipt is advisory-only. An explicit
+`degraded-single-host` fallback is local DONE assurance through host-verdict
+evidence, not direct or managed REVIEW evidence, and cannot borrow either
+reviewer authority path.
+
+## Operator guidance
+
+`lattice dispatch` prints two explicit execution modes. A native subagent uses
+its host lifecycle. A cross-provider CLI reviewer must use `host_run
+--managedReview`; raw `bash + codex/claude/agy` is advisory-only and cannot
+satisfy the managed evidence path.
+
+Poll the same run with `host_run_status --waitMs 30000`. Continue observing the
+same run across silent intervals. Cancel only on an explicit operator decision.
+Start a replacement only after an authoritative terminal and only when its
+cleanup proves replacement safety.
+
+## Retention and trust boundary
+
+`lattice doctor` reports worker liveness, provider-progress observability,
+deadline/cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. Explicit
+`doctor --repair` garbage-collects heavy terminal run directories only beyond
+90 days and first revalidates sealed spec, result, event-journal, proposal and
+evidence-binding digests, then preserves the minimal receipt plus evidence-binding
+digest under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. Any mismatch is reported as
+corrupt and retained for manual review. Active or corrupt runs and
+runs that still contain one-shot inputs are retained fail-closed. Failed startup
+removes one-shot secrets immediately.
+
+The local filesystem boundary does not defend against a same-UID or root
+attacker. Retained output may contain sensitive provider text and must be
+treated accordingly.
+
+## Compatibility and non-goals
+
+- Existing finite provider timeouts, cross-host policy ceilings, bounded retry
+  and fail-closed classifications remain in force.
+- Ordinary non-review host runs remain compatible but now gain durable
+  ownership and shared admission.
+- No remote scheduler, daemon, queue or native-host subagent abstraction is
+  introduced.
+- Usage diagnostics remain non-authoritative and never become lifecycle proof.

+- This mode does **not** change how normal Proofbound gate reviewers (`lattice-review-*`) work,
+  but their evidence authority depends on the invocation path. A registered host adapter can
+  issue a signed, exact native-review invocation attestation; that broker-attested native
+  reviewer may call `review_pass_set`, `finding_add`, or `delivery_check_set` directly. A
+  cross-provider reviewer launched through ManagedHostRun must instead submit its provider-owned
+  proposal and let `managed_review_evidence_import` write the pass/finding after the successful

 ## Out of Scope
 
 This design does not solve:
 
-- cryptographic identity or unforgeable agent identity
+- general human/agent identity outside the registered host-adapter attestation and managed receipt boundaries
 - cross-clone distributed locking
-- reviewer identity attestation
+- distributed reviewer identity attestation across machines or clones
 - malicious local users editing JSON by hand
 - replacing git as source of truth
 
 Those require a stronger trust model and should be separate work.
 
 ## Acceptance Criteria
 
 1. Two sessions mutating the same story: second session is rejected with owner guidance.

 ### M0 — Threat model + key-management decision doc  [doc · small · high-leverage]
 Objective: define, before any run, what makes the quorum sound.
 - How host A trusts host B's signing public key (a pinned `[hostId → publicKey]` manifest; out-of-band).
 - The **independence definition** and its honest boundary: cross-vendor (different companies/models)
   vs. same-operator orchestration — the paper may only claim what the setup earns.
 - Replay / stale-materialHash / supersession defenses; key rotation/revocation.
 Deliverable: `docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md`.
 Acceptance: names the trust anchor, the independence claim + its ceiling, and every fail-closed rule.
 Repro-first: exempt (documentation, not material code).
 
 ### M1 — Automatic cross-host review + disagreement surfacing (crypto-deferred)  [build · medium · the mechanism crux]
 Decision (2026-07-03): M1 is **crypto-deferred**. On the current single-machine, same-operator
 setup, tamper-proofing (signed verdicts / pinned keys) defends against a non-existent adversary —
 the value we can earn today is the **adversarial joint decision**, not a signature. So M1 builds the
 collection+decision mechanism now and defers the provenance crypto to M-crypto (below,
 external-skeptic-only).
+
+**Current-state supersession:** the bullets below preserve M1's historical
+direct-capture design. Production `cross_host_review` now launches/resumes one
+ManagedHostRun, and host-B provenance is the sealed terminal `receiptId` plus
+exact `managedRunId`; the old stdoutDigest-only direct capture is retired.
+Interrupt/TERM/KILL/reap ownership belongs to that ManagedHostRun supervisor,
+not to the cross-host controller or caller.
 Objective: turn the manual 2-host quorum into an **automatic** cross-host adversarial review that
 records a materialHash-bound host-B verdict through the existing capture path and surfaces where
 host A (Claude) and host B (Codex) disagree.
 - A new `cross_host_review` command auto-runs Codex as an independent **read-only** reviewer over the
   current materialHash-bound change (stdin-piped `codex exec -s read-only -C <worktree>`; parse ONLY
   the structured JSON verdict, record only a `stdoutDigest` for provenance — never raw stdout).
 - Fail-closed: no parseable/schema-valid verdict → `blocked` (`codex_review_no_parseable_verdict`);
   a verdict bound to a different materialHash → `blocked` (`codex_review_material_mismatch`).
 - Capture the host-B verdict via the existing `submitLocalVerdict` path (binds `materialDigest`,
   appends a `host_verdict` event) with a distinct derived hostId/session/key so the two hosts do not
   collapse in `groupByIndependentHost`.
 - `diffFindings` + `jointDecision` (pure): the joint decision is `pass` IFF both hosts pass AND there
   is no finding-level divergence; otherwise `blocked`, surfacing WHICH finding one host raised and the
   other missed (the gap `summarizeVerdicts` does not fill — it only counts pass/fail hosts).
 - Dispatch policy gains a NARROW `allowReviewOnlyRealHostSubprocess` flag that permits ONLY a
   read-only Codex reviewer; the general `allowRealHostSubprocess` implementation path for codex, and
   gemini/antigravity, stay refused.
 Files: `core/codex-review-leaf.ts` (new), `core/cross-host-review.ts` (new),
 `handlers/cross-host-review.ts` (new), `core/dispatch-policy.ts`, `cli/command-catalog.ts`,
 `registry.ts`. Crypto files (`receipt-bundle.ts`/`authority-signing.ts`) are explicitly **untouched**.
 Acceptance: with an injected fake Codex seam, a `fail` verdict carrying a host-B-only finding yields

docs/requirements/decisions/review-run-binding-race.md:4:When reviewer lanes run in parallel, or a reviewer retries review_run_start, a second run_start on the same (storyId, lane) in the same reviewRound mints a newer reviewRunId. currentRunForLane (review-run.ts) returns the newest-by-recency run, and any review_pass_set / finding_add bound to the ORIGINAL run is hard-rejected — at write time by assertCurrentReviewRunForEvidence (review-run.ts:669-672, "is not the current latest reviewer run") and at validate time by validateEvidenceRunBinding (review-run.ts:794-804, issue 'stale_run') — purely because a newer run exists, even though the bound run is still in the current round and still material- and scope-fresh. This empties the lane's valid-pass set and stalls quorum_submit (handlers/quorum-submit.ts), which forced a whole fresh REVIEW round during B-70e4. reviewerWrite is lease-exempt (command-policy.ts) and review_run_start vs review_pass_set/finding_add hold DISTINCT mkdir locks, so the owner lease never serialized these writers; B-77ed only raised the lock budget to 30s, which does not address the false-reject.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-run-binding-race.md:7:Remove the id-recency rejection: a non-latest run is ACCEPTED when it is still material-fresh and scope-fresh, and rejected only by the existing freshness and scope checks (stale-by-material/scope, never stale-merely-by-id). The validate-side relax is KIND-AWARE: the 'stale_run' issue is dropped only for evidence.kind === 'pass' (so a material-fresh non-latest PASS becomes valid), but KEPT for findings so an older OPEN finding is still surfaced and not hidden by a newer pass on the same lane (collectReviewerEvidenceState supersedes it only once the finding is resolved/dismissed). This is conditioned on a mandatory soundness guard added to checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit: the storyFilesHash drift-advisory downgrade must treat EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH (sha256 of an empty story-owned diff) as no-signal on BOTH the stored and the live side and fall through to strict materialHash, exactly as delivery-check-hash.ts:184-188 already does. The lease-contract doc (session-ownership-and-write-leases.md) is reconciled doc-only.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-run-binding-race.md:9:## Why id-recency is redundant
docs/requirements/decisions/review-run-binding-race.md:10:Both surviving checks compare the run's CAPTURED SNAPSHOT against the LIVE current state, never run-1 against run-2: checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit reads currentMaterialHash / currentStoryFilesHash from live HEAD; compareScopeBinding re-digests the live contract and the live main...HEAD diff pack. A second run_start changes only the reviewRunId, not what was reviewed; two same-round runs that captured the same tree are byte-identical to the live comparison. Round, lane, signature (verifyReviewRun), and workspace-binding checks all still fire.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-run-binding-race.md:13:The adversarial soundness review found that the storyFilesHash drift-advisory branch — the sole path where whole-tree material drift does not hard-reject — lacked the EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH no-signal guard. currentStoryFilesHash returns a truthy sha256('') for an empty story diff; under relax, a same-round run captured with an empty story diff could ride the advisory under arbitrary whole-tree drift while a newer run captured the real current state. The mandatory EMPTY guard closes this for all checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit callers.

docs/requirements/decisions/review-run-binding-race.md:16:- keep-strict: preserves the quorum-blocking false-reject for a check that adds no soundness.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-run-binding-race.md:17:- unify-lock-A alone: does NOT fix the race — a legitimate later run_start still invalidates an earlier fresh pass under strict id-recency; it only narrows the interleave window. Deferred as an optional follow-up.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-run-binding-race.md:18:- blanket relax (both kinds) without the EMPTY guard and without kind-awareness: unsound under empty-set storyFilesHash drift, AND it hides open findings behind a newer pass. Both were caught by a red->spike->story spike plus the adversarial design review, which is why the validate-side relax is kind-aware and the EMPTY guard is mandatory.

docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:3:Date: 2026-06-13
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:7:This document defines the execution plan for keeping Proofbound workflow commands

docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:13:suggestions from teaching agents that ordinary Proofbound lifecycle commands belong
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:14:to a Codex-specific namespace.

docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:23:## Problem Statement
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:25:Proofbound is the workflow layer. It coordinates story state, checklist state,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:26:review artifacts, validation evidence, delivery checks, and convergence checks
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:27:across hosts. Those commands must remain host-neutral.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:29:Codex is one possible host/adapter. Codex-specific commands may diagnose or
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:30:verify Codex adapter assets, but they must not become a second namespace for
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:31:ordinary Proofbound workflow operations.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:33:The operator-facing defect has two closely related forms:

docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-codex-command-boundary-execution-plan.md:39:  host-neutral mental model even when the command technically works.

docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:9:When a Claude host started Codex (or a Codex host started Claude) with raw shell

docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:13:as failure caused duplicate reviewer launches; treating `running` forever as
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:14:proof of health caused unbounded waits. Output silence alone answers neither
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:17:Proofbound is host-neutral. Native Codex/Claude subagent lifecycle APIs are not
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:18:portable and therefore are not the execution contract. This decision covers
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:19:only Proofbound-owned cross-provider CLI processes.

docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:47:## State and liveness contract
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:49:The states are `submitted`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:50:`timed_out`. Exactly one terminal file wins by exclusive creation. Repeated
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:51:status, cancel and resume operations are idempotent and never create a new run.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:53:Two clocks are deliberately distinct:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:55:- `workerHeartbeatAt` shows that the supervisor can still update its durable
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:56:  snapshot;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:57:- `lastProviderProgressAt` changes only when observable provider stdout/stderr
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:60:Neither clock is a completion oracle. A provider may legitimately be silent,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:61:and a worker heartbeat does not prove provider progress. Expiry of a 30-second
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:62:observation wait is non-terminal: it only wakes the caller and never authorizes
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:63:a retry. The `host_run_status` call is also the run's next-touch reconciler,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:64:however, so during that call an already-requested cancellation or an expired
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:65:absolute deadline can legitimately publish the corresponding `cancelled` or
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:66:`timed_out` terminal state.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:68:Every run has a finite absolute deadline (30 minutes by default, bounded to 24
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:69:hours). Deadline or cancellation reconciliation performs bounded TERM, KILL,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:70:reap and residual probing. Replacement is safe only when cleanup facts prove
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:71:there is no residual process group. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity remains
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:72:`replacementSafe=false`; it is not guessed away.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:74:## Persistence and process ownership
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:76:Each run has a 0700 directory at
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:77:`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:78:primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:79:DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:80:bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:81:capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:82:Prompt, capability and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot inputs;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:83:the worker validates and deletes them before provider launch. Only root and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:84:runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:86:On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Codex receives the
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:87:prompt through documented stdin (`codex exec ... -`) and Claude receives a 0600
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:88:one-shot prompt file. The current agy print launcher accepts prompt text only in
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:89:argv, so managed agy execution refuses before provider spawn until agy exposes a
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:90:stdin or protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms likewise refuse
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:91:before provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup is equivalent.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:93:## Shared provider admission
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:95:Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:96:of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:97:token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:98:Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:99:not process admission.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:101:A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:102:reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:103:checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:104:already been reclaimed and reassigned.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:106:Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:107:admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:108:review evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:110:## Formal managed reviewer evidence
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:112:Native-host reviewers retain the existing signed ReviewRun plus direct
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:113:ReviewPass/Finding flow. A cross-provider CLI reviewer uses a two-phase flow:
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:115:1. The controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:116:2. `host_run --managedReview` derives the exact assembled prompt and seals
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:117:   story, provider, lane, ReviewRun, head, material, story-files and prompt
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:118:   bindings.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:119:3. The managed prompt requires the provider's final assistant result to be one
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:120:   bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope with
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:121:   pass-or-findings and truthful read evidence. It cannot write final
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:122:   `review_pass_set`/`finding_add` evidence from inside the managed run. After a
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:123:   successful provider exit, the owning adapter selects only Codex's terminal
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:124:   `item.completed` `agent_message` or Claude's terminal `result`; tool logs,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:125:   arbitrary stdout and controller fields are never proposal inputs. The worker
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:126:   validates the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple and atomically writes
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:127:   the immutable proposal. Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized final
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:128:   envelopes fail the managed run closed. The older descriptor-authorized
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:129:   `managed_review_proposal_set` callback remains compatibility-only.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:130:4. Successful terminal creation seals spec, proposal, result and event-journal
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:131:   digests plus cleanup facts.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:132:5. The controller calls `managed_review_evidence_import` with only the exact
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:133:   runId and receiptId. It cannot provide or alter verdict bytes.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:134:6. The importer preserves provider reviewer/lane/ReviewRun/read provenance and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:135:   writes the existing signed ReviewPass/Finding shape.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:136:7. Import time and the REVIEW gate both call the shared Proof Admissibility
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:137:   registry/intake/evaluator and revalidate the current terminal, proposal,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:138:   journal, prompt and material tuple.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:140:Raw CLI output outside the trusted final-result adapter lane, usage-ledger rows, time-window correlations, pre-terminal
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:141:proposals, failed/cancelled/timed-out terminals and controller-authored verdicts
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:142:cannot upgrade to managed reviewer evidence. Raw same-UID CLI calls, forged
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:143:environment values, stale process groups, terminal/reaped runs and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:144:ambiguous/multiple active candidates cannot borrow the descriptor authority.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:146:The authority classifications remain disjoint. A native-host reviewer keeps the
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:147:signed ReviewRun plus direct ReviewPass/Finding path only when a registered
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:148:host-adapter broker signs the exact closeout invocation. Its Ed25519 attestation
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:149:binds Story, agent/lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:150:adapter/host identity and a one-shot nonce. Lattice stores the registered public
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:151:key and nonce-consumption record, but exposes no issuer command and stores no
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:152:broker private key. `dispatch`, `review_run_start`, inherited environment values
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:153:and raw provider CLIs cannot mint this authority. The host adapter must inject
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:154:the signed attestation over a dedicated descriptor for the exact CLI process;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:155:without that integration, native direct evidence is advisory-only and formal
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:156:review must use the managed path.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:158:Process ancestry is secondary evidence. An unobservable process table, as in a
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:159:brokered desktop sandbox, does not negate a valid broker signature. When a full
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:160:ancestry is observable, any mixed distinct provider families (Claude→Codex or
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:161:Codex→Claude) veto direct evidence even if the nearest ancestor matches. The
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:162:one-shot local nonce ledger prevents replay but is not represented as protection
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:163:against a same-UID/root attacker capable of replacing trusted configuration or
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:164:instrumenting the broker.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:166:A cross-provider CLI reviewer requires a managed terminal receipt;
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:167:cross-provider CLI output without that receipt is advisory-only. An explicit
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:168:`degraded-single-host` fallback is local DONE assurance through host-verdict
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:169:evidence, not direct or managed REVIEW evidence, and cannot borrow either
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:170:reviewer authority path.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:172:## Operator guidance
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:174:`lattice dispatch` prints two explicit execution modes. A native subagent uses
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:175:its host lifecycle. A cross-provider CLI reviewer must use `host_run
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:176:--managedReview`; raw `bash + codex/claude/agy` is advisory-only and cannot
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:177:satisfy the managed evidence path.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:179:Poll the same run with `host_run_status --waitMs 30000`. Continue observing the
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:180:same run across silent intervals. Cancel only on an explicit operator decision.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:181:Start a replacement only after an authoritative terminal and only when its
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:182:cleanup proves replacement safety.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:186:`lattice doctor` reports worker liveness, provider-progress observability,
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:187:deadline/cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. Explicit
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:188:`doctor --repair` garbage-collects heavy terminal run directories only beyond
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:189:90 days and first revalidates sealed spec, result, event-journal, proposal and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:190:evidence-binding digests, then preserves the minimal receipt plus evidence-binding
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:191:digest under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. Any mismatch is reported as
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:192:corrupt and retained for manual review. Active or corrupt runs and
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:193:runs that still contain one-shot inputs are retained fail-closed. Failed startup
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:194:removes one-shot secrets immediately.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:196:The local filesystem boundary does not defend against a same-UID or root
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:197:attacker. Retained output may contain sensitive provider text and must be
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:198:treated accordingly.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:200:## Compatibility and non-goals
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:202:- Existing finite provider timeouts, cross-host policy ceilings, bounded retry
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:203:  and fail-closed classifications remain in force.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:204:- Ordinary non-review host runs remain compatible but now gain durable
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:205:  ownership and shared admission.
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:206:- No remote scheduler, daemon, queue or native-host subagent abstraction is
docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md:208:- Usage diagnostics remain non-authoritative and never become lifecycle proof.

docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-execution-plan.md:35:## 1. What this closes and what it proves
docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-execution-plan.md:37:Today all evidence (Tier-A engine contract, Tier-B powered ablation) is produced on one operator's

docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-execution-plan.md:60:### M1 — Automatic cross-host review + disagreement surfacing (crypto-deferred)  [build · medium · the mechanism crux]

README.md:5:[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Proof-or-Stop/Prooforstop)](https://github.com/Proof-or-Stop/Prooforstop/releases/latest)
README.md:7:> An evidence-gated control layer for unattended agent development — every phase advance, review pass, and "done" must present fresh, code-state-bound, mechanically verifiable proof, or the loop stops.
README.md:9:**Proof-or-Stop** is an evidence-gated control layer that lets coding agents run an unattended development loop — *plan → execute → review → reflect → done* — where every step forward is admitted only on **mechanically verifiable evidence bound to the current code state**, never on the agent's word. If the evidence isn't there, the loop repairs or stops. The point isn't that an agent *can* run unattended — plenty of frameworks do that. The point is that what an unattended run marks "done" comes with a **mechanically checkable merge-readiness claim** — evidence a reviewer or merge policy can act on.
README.md:11:The host-neutral evidence boundary is formalized as the **Evidence Environment
README.md:12:Adapter (EEA)** contract: an Agent proposes, an Environment observes, Proof
README.md:13:Admissibility evaluates, and the existing Gate decides. The current
README.md:14:implementation includes the generic contract plus bounded code-runtime and
README.md:15:Quantum receipt projections; the existing DONE_REQUIRED lifecycle evaluator
README.md:16:consumes the code-runtime projection after revalidating its raw bindings. It
README.md:17:does not expose an arbitrary runner; Lean,
README.md:18:Rosetta, AlphaFold, PINN solvers, browsers, databases, CI, Kubernetes, and
README.md:19:production deployment remain integration targets.
README.md:24:plan ──▶ execute ──▶ review ──▶ reflect ──▶ done
README.md:26:  └──────────  proof, or stop  ◀─────────────┘
README.md:29:## The problem: "done" is a claim, not a proof
README.md:31:Agents write code, run tests, and report `tests passed / reviewed / done` on their own — and downstream automation (merge, release, next task) takes those words at face value. But they are **claims, not evidence**:
README.md:33:- tests may have run against **stale code**;
README.md:34:- a "LGTM" may have **no auditable artifact** behind it;
README.md:35:- a green pipeline can **coexist with a real defect** (the *green-but-wrong* failure).
README.md:37:The most expensive incident is the quiet one: **tests green, code wrong, auto-merged to main.**
README.md:41:Any lifecycle advance — next phase, review pass, mark done, merge-readiness claim — **must** be backed by structured evidence that is **fresh** (still bound to the current code-state hash — the moment code changes, prior evidence is void) and **tamper-evident** (signed, not hand-waved). No qualifying evidence → **repair, downgrade, or stop.** Never pass on the agent's testimony.
README.md:43:> Think of it less as a better engine and more as a traffic light for autonomous development: the value isn't speed — it's making "the wrong thing auto-merges to main" *mechanically hard to happen*.
README.md:47:Seven kinds of proof, each mapped to the evidence behind it:
README.md:49:| # | Proof | What it establishes | Evidence |
README.md:51:| 1 | **Formal** | when a claim is *admissible* is precisely defined | admissibility predicate + gated lifecycle-transition equations |
README.md:52:| 2 | **Mechanism** | the gate's verdict can't be faked or gamed | freshness binding, anti-forgery, receipt verification; **10/10** engine contract (zero false DONE); **18** tamper classes rejected (zero false accepts) |
README.md:53:| 3 | **System** | the method is really implemented, not just theory | Proofbound runs it as a full autonomous coding lifecycle (PLAN→DEV→REVIEW→TEST→DONE) |
README.md:54:| 4 | **Empirical** | stronger control *causally* reduces amplification | 9,240-cell powered ablation; pre-registered primary **A4 vs A2′: 31/1800 → 2/1800** (≈1.6pp, CI excludes zero) |
README.md:55:| 5 | **Failure** | missing or wrong evidence → repair or safe-stop, never a false DONE | injected-failure runs exhibit repair / safe-stop / no-false-DONE |
README.md:56:| 6 | **Operational** | it works in real, sustained lifecycle use | self-application corpus: **565 stories / 1,007 findings**; **26/28 (93%)** deep-set findings from independent review while the author's tests were green |
README.md:57:| 7 | **Boundary** | it states honestly what is *not* proven | threats / future work: no general PR-less auto-merge; cross-vendor quorum & multi-model generalization remain open |
README.md:59:![Amplified test-passing-but-wrong deliverables per 1,000 injected cells: A1 single-pass ≈9, A2 naive-retry ≈10, A2′ budget-capped retry ≈17, A3 retry with advisory review ≈8, A4 retry with the enforced gate ≈1.](docs/assets/fig-gate-ablation.png)
README.md:61:The empirical result's sharpest cut is **enforcement, not review**: given the *same* review signal, treating it as advisory (A3) lets 14 defects through while enforcing it (A4) lets only 2 — at nearly identical token spend (A3/A4 = 0.98×). And "green tests ≠ correct" is common, not rare: in the deep set, 93% of findings came from independent review while the author's own tests were green.
README.md:63:## Where it fits
README.md:65:**Proof-or-Stop specializes evidence-gated claim admissibility for autonomous coding lifecycles.** What sets it apart is the combination:
README.md:67:- **No admissible evidence → no lifecycle advance.**
README.md:68:- Agent / reviewer / tool output is a **claim**, not truth.
README.md:69:- Evidence must be **mechanically checkable** — structured, not prose.
README.md:70:- Evidence must be **bound to current state** — `materialHash` / `headHash` / `storyFilesHash` / `policyHash` / `commandSetHash`.
README.md:71:- The gate controls specific **transitions** — PLAN→DEV, REVIEW→TEST, TEST→DONE, handoff, merge-readiness.
README.md:72:- Failure is not an infinite loop — **repair / degrade honestly / escalate / stop safely.**
README.md:73:- **Host-neutral** — host identity affects provenance and independence, not gate semantics.
README.md:75:## What it does *not* do
README.md:78:- It does **not** make development faster — on a clean task it's roughly **2× pure overhead**.
README.md:79:- It does **not** replace your merge policy — the gate yields a **merge-readiness claim**; the actual merge stays a repo/human decision.
README.md:80:- Cross-vendor quorum and multi-model generalization are **still future work**;
README.md:81:  the Evidence Environment quorum path is explicitly fail-closed unsupported
README.md:82:  until a project-owned pinned-key, session-bound, revocation-aware producer
README.md:85:Its job is narrow and expensive-to-skip: turn the costliest failure — *wrong code silently reaching main* — into something mechanically difficult.

docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:146:1. The first story-scoped mutating command for a story acquires the owner lease.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:147:2. The lease records `sessionId`, hostname, pid, cwd, command, `acquiredAt`, `heartbeatAt`, and optional human label.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:148:3. Owner commands refresh `heartbeatAt`.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:149:4. Non-owner story-scoped mutating commands fail closed.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:150:5. Read-only commands do not require a lease and do not refresh ownership.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:151:6. Lease is released when the story reaches DONE or DISCARDED and cleanup succeeds.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:152:7. Lease may be marked stale after 30 minutes without heartbeat.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:153:8. A stale lease can be taken over with explicit `--takeover`, recording an event.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:154:9. A non-stale lease requires explicit `--forceTakeover` and should be treated as human-approved.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:158:1. Main/shared mutations must acquire a global mkdir-style lock.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:159:2. The lock must be atomic and stale-reclaimable.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:160:3. The lock scope must cover the whole critical section, not just the final write.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:161:4. DONE must hold the main write lock from pre-merge final check through merge and worktree cleanup.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:162:5. B-META finding writes must hold the main write lock and perform idempotency checks inside the lock.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:163:6. Lock acquisition failure is blocking. Proofbound must not proceed optimistically.

docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:257:## Read-Only Reviewer Mode (`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1`)
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:259:The command classes above describe ownership coordination between *owner sessions*. A separate
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:260:concern is **advisory external reviewers**: external Claude/Codex/Gemini processes delegated
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:261:to inspect artifacts and return structured findings as text — they are not Proofbound gate
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:262:reviewers and must not write lifecycle evidence directly.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:264:`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` is an opt-in guard for these advisory reviewer processes. It
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:265:layers on top of the `CommandPolicy` / owner-lease architecture:
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:267:- The guard runs **before** `enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate` and before preCommand hooks, so a
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:268:  readonly reviewer cannot acquire an owner lease, use `--takeover`, or trigger any hook
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:269:  side-effect that requires mutating access.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:270:- Only `ownershipClass === 'readOnly'` commands (e.g. `session_brief`, `story_get`,
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:271:  `checklist_get`, `finding_list`) proceed. All other classes fail closed.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:272:- This mode does **not** change how normal Proofbound gate reviewers (`lattice-review-*`) work,
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:273:  but their evidence authority depends on the invocation path. A registered host adapter can
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:274:  issue a signed, exact native-review invocation attestation; that broker-attested native
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:275:  reviewer may call `review_pass_set`, `finding_add`, or `delivery_check_set` directly. A
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:276:  cross-provider reviewer launched through ManagedHostRun must instead submit its provider-owned
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:277:  proposal and let `managed_review_evidence_import` write the pass/finding after the successful
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:278:  terminal receipt is sealed. Raw provider CLI processes and unregistered adapters are
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:279:  advisory-only and cannot directly author gate evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:281:This section is the current active contract for reviewer read-only mode. Older
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:282:reviewer-role background may describe the same separation concept, but must not
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:283:override the `LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` env name or the command class rules
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md:284:documented here.

docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:10:Proofbound should add a mandatory review assurance floor for code-changing stories: ordinary code diffs require at least one review round before DONE, failure or bug signals escalate to three local single-host rounds, and high-risk lifecycle/gate/Authority/process-fact work keeps the stronger three-round two-host or explicit degraded-single-host path.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:12:## Context
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:14:A small development task can look low risk during PLAN but still ship a bug when it reaches DONE with no review floor. Existing review escalation is threshold-triggered by first REVIEW round countable findings, which is useful but does not prevent zero-review code closure. This plan documents the missing floor and the escalation rule without implementing runtime code in this story.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:18:Applies to future Proofbound CLI lifecycle policy and DONE closure design for code-changing stories. This document is a planning and policy artifact only; runtime DONE oracle implementation, storage fields, and exact row ids are future work.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:22:- Do not force every code-changing story into three rounds by default.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:23:- Do not weaken existing review_escalation_status, decision_doc_quorum_check, or DONE gates.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:24:- Do not claim local 3x1 review is two-host independent review.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:25:- Do not claim Authority completion without verified Authority Server gate_decision receipts.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:26:- Do not implement runtime gate code in this story.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:28:## Options Considered
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:30:### Force every code change through three local single-host rounds
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:34:- Stronger than one-round review for every code diff
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:38:- Raises token and time cost without requiring a real failure signal
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:40:### Keep current threshold-triggered review escalation only
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:43:- No new policy or implementation work
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:44:- Preserves current lifecycle behavior
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:47:- Does not solve zero-review code DONE
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:48:- Misses low-risk-looking tasks that only reveal bugs after implementation
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:50:### Require full 3x2 for every code change
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:54:- Reduces reliance on single-host judgment
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:57:- Too expensive for ordinary small code changes
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:58:- Can block local development when a second host is unavailable
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:62:Introduce a review assurance floor: zero-review code DONE is invalid; clean ordinary code requires at least one review round; real failure signals such as validation fail, bug, verified reviewer finding, post-DONE regression, or repeated rework make 3x1 local single-host audit sticky for closure; high-risk gate/Authority/lifecycle/process-fact work still requires 3x2 unless explicit degraded-single-host evidence is recorded.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:64:## Operational Rules
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:66:- If a story has no material code diff, it may use the existing docs/typo/annotation policy for one-round low-risk review.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:67:- If a story has a material code diff, DONE must require at least one review round over the current material hash.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:68:- If a story records a validation fail, bug, verified reviewer finding, post-DONE regression, or repeated rework signal, DONE must require three rounds x one local host unless stronger policy requires 3x2.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:69:- Failure-triggered 3x1 escalation must be sticky for the story material until DONE or an explicit approved fallback supersedes it.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:70:- Lifecycle, gate, Authority, review, and process-fact work remains high-risk and should use three rounds x two hosts, or an explicit degraded-single-host fallback when policy allows.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:71:- Local host verdicts and degraded fallback evidence are Non-authority evidence and must not set authorityDone, fullAuthorityDone, or productionDone.
docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md:72:- Future implementation must fail closed on stale material hash, missing host identity, missing prompt or validation binding, and duplicate/self-claimed assurance.

docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:143:## 8. Host keyword proposal contract
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:145:### 8.1 Default host policy
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:147:- Primary proposers: Codex CLI and Claude Code CLI.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:148:- Supplemental proposer: Antigravity CLI (`agy`) when the two primary hosts disagree materially, candidate ambiguity remains, either primary host is unavailable/quota-limited, or the reviewer explicitly requests a third semantic perspective.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:149:- No host proposal can expand lifecycle authority or satisfy a gate.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:151:### 8.2 Fresh-context input
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:153:The CLI first applies one pre-egress sanitizer to every field and artifact that could enter a host prompt. There is no alternate adapter path around this boundary. The sanitizer:
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:155:- transmits identifier, command, configuration, and environment-variable names, never detected values;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:156:- redacts secret-like values in Story/checklist prose, backticks, error payloads, paths, titles, symbols, seeds, and memory-derived text;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:157:- hashes or omits sensitive provenance and `sourceRef` values while retaining a local-only mapping for audit;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:158:- rejects and records unsafe host inputs or outputs instead of trying to repair them;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:159:- treats uncertain classification as sensitive and skips the host call, continuing with deterministic local routing;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:160:- persists only the sanitized request digest and sanitized proposal artifact.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:162:After sanitization, each host receives only:
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:164:- Story ID, title, description, keywords, and risk signals;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:165:- checklist title, `userSees`, `excludes`, and related-doc paths;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:166:- deterministic seed list with provenance;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:167:- changed files/symbols when available;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:168:- complete decisions filename/title index, without document bodies;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:169:- proposal budget and output schema.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:171:The host does not receive the entire requirements corpus, the owner's full conversation, raw secret-bearing metadata, or the local-only provenance map.

docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:312:The router MUST escalate instead of guessing when any condition holds:

docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:408:## 17. Quality floor
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:410:The rollout cannot claim success from token reduction alone. Required evaluation sets:

docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:413:2. Negative controls: similarly named but irrelevant historical plans.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:414:3. Gate/process changes: cases that must escalate.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:415:4. Global rename cases.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:416:5. Candidate cutoff ties and host disagreement.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:417:6. Memory no-hit and host-unavailable paths.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:418:7. Prompt-injection documents.
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:419:8. Corpus mutation between route and review.

docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:424:- known-relevant document recall: at least 98% overall;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:425:- no loss of load-bearing findings versus the full-scan baseline suite;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:426:- false candidate rate reported, not hidden;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:427:- default full-read count at most 8;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:428:- P95 routing latency target under 5 seconds excluding host latency;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:429:- default prompt/document bytes at least 90% below full-corpus baseline;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:430:- full-scan rate measured and justified, not optimized to zero;
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:431:- zero accepted manifest/read-log mismatches.

docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:538:## 20. Validation matrix
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:540:| Scenario | Expected result |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:542:| Exact related doc | rank 1 with explicit-path reason |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:543:| Sparse matches | retain deterministic seeds, record low coverage, and escalate when the source-class floor is not met |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:544:| Noisy/excessive matches | deduplicate and rank within configured result budgets; truncation that can change the cutoff escalates |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:545:| Zero-candidate result | record the empty result and ambiguity reason, then use bounded escalation; never silently inject or fully scan the corpus |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:546:| Legacy synonym proposed by one host | local hit enters candidates with host provenance |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:547:| Both hosts miss exact config key | deterministic seed still retrieves document |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:548:| Codex/Claude disagree at cutoff | ambiguity escalation |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:549:| `agy` unavailable | primary pair continues; availability recorded |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:550:| Both primary hosts unavailable | deterministic path continues; no automatic full scan |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:552:| High-risk gate change | recorded broad-scan escalation |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:553:| Irrelevant 5 MB Markdown file | absent from full reads and prompt bytes |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:554:| Relevant document ranked ninth with tied score | cutoff tie escalates |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:555:| Corpus changes after routing | artifact stale; reroute required |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:556:| Manifest claims unread file | fail closed |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:557:| Mechanical log contains undeclared full read | fail closed |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:558:| Prompt-injection text in document | ignored as instruction; content remains evidence only |
docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:559:| Proposal exceeds schema budget | proposal rejected and recorded |

docs/requirements/decisions/multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:561:| Secret in seed provenance, `sourceRef`, path/title, config, or error metadata | value is hashed or omitted from host-bound and persisted artifacts; the raw mapping stays local only |
