docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:8:## Problem Statement
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:10:Proofbound can launch or coordinate work through multiple LLM-capable hosts, but it
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:11:does not yet have one consistent place to record what each model call consumed,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:12:what budget decision was made before the call, and whether final usage came from
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:13:the provider, from a local prompt-size estimate, or from no reliable source at
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:16:Without a usage ledger, future budget decisions risk mixing three different
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:17:facts:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:19:- true provider-reported usage returned by the model provider;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:20:- approximate prompt-size estimates made before or around a request;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:21:- unavailable usage when neither the provider nor a trusted adapter reports
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:24:The ledger must keep these categories mechanically distinct. A local estimate is
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:25:useful for preflight safety, but it is not billing truth, receipt truth, or
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:26:Authority evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:30:1. Do not optimize for optimization.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:32:3. Only fix real correctness issues.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:33:4. Follow consistency of logic across providers, hosts, and Authority modes.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:34:5. Preserve the existing Proofbound boundary: local workflow evidence is local
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:35:   unless a future receipt-backed Authority path explicitly promotes it.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:39:- Add a future JSONL ledger for LLM usage events that can be appended by local
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:40:  Proofbound surfaces and, later, by receipt-backed Authority execution.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:41:- Represent true provider-reported usage, approximate prompt-size estimates, and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:42:  unavailable usage as separate states.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:43:- Support preflight and postflight budget decisions without treating estimates
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:44:  as final usage.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:45:- Keep local Non-authority mode usable for ordinary Proofbound workflow while still
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:46:  recording budget refusals and available usage facts.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:47:- Define the Authority Server receipt-backed path for future production
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:48:  accounting without overclaiming local authority.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:49:- Prevent raw prompt, raw transcript, provider secret, customer API key, actor
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:50:  key, and authorization header material from entering ledger records.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:54:- No source code change in this story.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:55:- No provider adapter rewrite.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:56:- No pricing optimizer, model router, or arbitrary cost-saving feature.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:57:- No token-perfect estimator. Estimates are bounded diagnostics and preflight
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:58:  guards only.

docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:60:  runners, or host transcripts.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:61:- No replacement for signed `AuthorityReceipt` gate evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:62:- No change to Authority Server receipt contracts in this story.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:66:The ledger record must carry a `usage.source` discriminator:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:68:| Source | Meaning | May count as final usage? | May satisfy Authority? |
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:70:| `provider-reported` | The provider response included usage counters or billing-relevant units returned by the provider adapter. | Yes, for local budget accounting and display. | Only when embedded in a future signed evidence envelope and covered by a verified Authority receipt. |
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:71:| `prompt-size-estimate` | Proofbound estimated prompt size before or around the request, using a local counter, tokenizer, bytes, or characters. | No. It may justify preflight refusal or warnings, but not final usage. | No. |
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:72:| `unavailable` | No trusted provider usage and no accepted estimate are available. | No. It records absence explicitly. | No. |
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:76:- Provider-reported usage wins over estimates for the same completed call.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:77:- Estimates must name the estimator and unit. They must not masquerade as
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:78:  provider token counts.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:80:- A failed request may still write a ledger entry if it consumed budget,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:81:  returned usage, or triggered a budget refusal.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:82:- Ledger readers must never infer that missing counts are zero-cost.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:84:### Estimate accuracy and fallback order
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:86:`prompt-size-estimate` records must use the most accurate available estimator,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:87:in a strict, explicitly ordered fallback chain:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:89:1. **Provider `count_tokens` endpoint (preferred).** When the provider exposes a
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:90:   token-counting endpoint, the estimate must prefer it. These counts are
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:91:   model-version-specific: the same text tokenizes differently across model
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:92:   versions, so the count must be requested for the exact target model.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:93:2. **Local tokenizer (fallback).** When the provider endpoint is unavailable,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:94:   fall back to a local tokenizer bound to the same provider/model family.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:95:3. **Bytes/characters heuristic (offline fallback only).** A bytes- or
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:96:   character-based heuristic is the lowest-confidence fallback and is used only
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:97:   when offline, i.e. when neither the provider endpoint nor a local tokenizer is
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:98:   available. It must never be promoted to the preferred estimator.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:100:Every estimate record must:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:102:- record `usage.estimator.confidence` as `high | medium | low`, reflecting which
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:103:  method was used (`high` for provider `count_tokens`, `medium` for a local
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:104:  tokenizer, `low` for the bytes/chars heuristic);
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:105:- bind the estimate to the exact `provider.model` it was computed for, because
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:106:  token counts are model-version-specific and an estimate for one model version
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:107:  must not be reused for another;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:108:- still record `usage.estimator.name`, `usage.estimator.version`, and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:109:  `usage.estimator.unit` alongside the new `confidence` field.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:111:### Streaming and failure usage capture
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:113:Streaming responses report final usage differently from non-streaming responses,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:116:- For streaming responses, final usage must be read from the terminal stream
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:117:  event (the final `message_delta` / final message that carries the completed
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:118:  `usage` object), not assumed from a non-streaming response shape. The usage on
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:119:  the terminal event is the authoritative provider-reported count for the call,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:120:  and it still qualifies as `usage.source=provider-reported`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:121:- A call that errors or times out mid-stream still records the partial output
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:122:  usage it actually consumed up to the failure point. An errored call that
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:123:  produced tokens still cost budget, so it must not be recorded as zero. If a
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:124:  terminal event with partial real counts was received, those partial counts are
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:125:  still `provider-reported`, not downgraded to an estimate.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:126:- `usage.source=unavailable` is set only when there is truly no count available —
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:127:  no terminal usage event and no partial counts. It must never be used as a
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:128:  shortcut, and missing usage must never be defaulted to `0` to pass a budget.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:130:This is consistent with the existing rule that a failed request may still write a
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:131:ledger entry when it consumed budget, returned usage, or triggered a refusal.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:133:## Ledger Path and Runtime Artifact Classification
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:135:The intended local ledger path is:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:137:```text

docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:141:This path is Proofbound runtime state. A future implementation must register it in
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:142:`packages/main/src/core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts` with semantics equivalent
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:145:- `id`: `llm-usage-ledger`;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:146:- `matchers`: exact `.lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl` or prefix
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:147:  `.lattice/usage/` if the writer later needs adjacent usage-runtime files;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:148:- `ignorePatterns`: `.lattice/usage/`;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:149:- `materialHash`: `exclude`;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:150:- `volatile`: `true`;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:151:- `repairableTrackedArtifact`: `true`;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:152:- description: local LLM usage diagnostic ledger for budget accounting and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:153:  operator diagnostics.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:155:The ledger is not process evidence, story evidence, validation evidence, or
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:156:gate-consumed proof. It may help operators understand local usage and budget
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:157:decisions, but it must not be read as lifecycle evidence under `.lattice/story/`
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:158:or as a replacement for signed Authority receipts. `doctor`, material-hash
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:159:calculation, runtime artifact repair, and gitignore management should treat it
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:160:the same way they treat other mutable runtime diagnostics under `.lattice/`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:162:## Call and Attempt Correlation Semantics
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:164:Ledger correlation must be stable before any provider request exists. The
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:165:writer must generate call identity locally before preflight estimation, and must
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:166:not use `provider.requestIdHash` as the primary key for estimates, blocked
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:167:refusals, or summaries.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:169:Required correlation fields:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:171:- `ledgerCallId`: stable id for one logical LLM call requested by Proofbound. It is
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:172:  generated before preflight budget checks and reused by all records for that
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:174:- `attemptId`: stable id for one execution attempt within a `ledgerCallId`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:175:  Retries reuse the same `ledgerCallId` and receive a new `attemptId`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:177:  `ledgerCallId` + `attemptId`. The preflight estimate is earlier than the
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:178:  blocked refusal, provider-reported final record, or unavailable final record
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:179:  for the same attempt.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:180:- `supersedesRecordIds`: explicit list of earlier `recordId` values replaced by
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:181:  this record for summary accounting. The field is required and may be empty.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:185:- A preflight estimate, blocked refusal, postflight provider-reported record,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:186:  and postflight unavailable record for the same attempt must share
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:187:  `ledgerCallId` and `attemptId`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:188:- A blocked refusal must keep the locally generated ids even though no provider
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:189:  request was sent and `provider.requestIdHash` is absent.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:190:- A provider-reported final record for an attempt must list the preflight
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:191:  estimate record id in `supersedesRecordIds` when both records exist.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:192:- A blocked refusal may list the preflight estimate record id in
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:193:  `supersedesRecordIds` when the refusal is the final decision for that
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:194:  attempt.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:195:- Ledger summaries must select the latest non-superseded accounting record per
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:196:  `ledgerCallId` + `attemptId` for decision counts.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:197:- Final usage totals must count provider-reported usage only once. They must
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:198:  exclude superseded prompt-size estimates for the same attempt once
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:199:  provider-reported final usage exists.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:200:- Estimates may still appear in a separate diagnostic estimate view, but that
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:201:  view must keep `usage.source=prompt-size-estimate` visible and must not merge
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:202:  estimates into final provider usage totals.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:203:- `provider.requestIdHash` is optional provider correlation metadata only. It is
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:204:  useful after a provider request exists, but it is not stable enough for
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:205:  preflight records, blocked records, or cross-source ledger summaries.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:209:Attribution fields (`storyId`, `phase`, `role`/`agentType`, and subagent ids)
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:210:must be captured at preflight — that is, at call time from the active
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:211:lease/session context — not reconstructed after the fact. Post-hoc attribution
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:212:drifts when a lease moves on or a session ends between the call and the write, so
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:213:the writer snapshots the active context before provider dispatch and binds it to
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:218:- `storyId` and `phase` are read from the active lease/session context at
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:219:  preflight and reused by every record for that `ledgerCallId`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:220:- Non-story calls (for example a global `validate` run or a background daemon)
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:221:  record `storyId=null`. They are NOT dropped: null-story usage is still real
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:222:  usage and must appear in summaries under a non-story bucket.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:223:- Subagent and nested calls propagate the parent `storyId` and `phase`, and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:224:  additionally record a subagent/thread identity (`subagentId` / `threadId`) so
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:225:  nested usage is traceable back to the parent story while staying
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:226:  distinguishable from the parent's own calls.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:227:- Every record carries a `role` / `agentType` field
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:228:  (`implementer | reviewer | main | ...`) captured at call time, so summaries can
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:229:  break down per-story usage by role.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:231:These fields never gate workflow; they are accounting and diagnostic
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:232:attribution only.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:236:Accuracy is not only per-record correctness; accuracy is completeness. A
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:237:perfectly shaped record is worthless if some provider calls never reach the
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:238:ledger at all. A dispatch path that bypasses the writer silently under-counts,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:239:and a silent under-count is indistinguishable from low usage. The plan therefore
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:240:treats completeness as a first-class correctness property.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:242:Single writer choke-point:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:244:- All provider dispatch must flow through a single ledger-writing choke-point.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:245:  There is exactly one code path that emits the provider request and the same
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:246:  path is responsible for emitting the ledger record(s) for that call. No
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:247:  provider call site may dispatch directly without going through this writer.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:248:- This makes completeness true by construction: if a call happened, the
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:249:  choke-point saw it, and a record was written (provider-reported, estimate,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:250:  blocked, or unavailable).
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:252:Periodic reconciliation:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:254:- A periodic reconciliation check compares the count of provider-dispatch events
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:255:  against the count of ledger final records, keyed per
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:256:  `ledgerCallId` + `attemptId`. Every dispatched attempt must resolve to exactly
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:257:  one final accounting record (provider-reported or unavailable) plus its
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:258:  earlier correlated records.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:259:- Any mismatch (a dispatch event with no corresponding ledger final record, or
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:260:  the reverse) surfaces a completeness gap for operator attention. The
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:261:  reconciliation surfaces gaps; it does not silently reconcile them away.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:262:- Reconciliation cannot run on `provider.requestIdHash` alone because blocked and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:263:  preflight records have no provider request; it uses the locally generated
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:264:  `ledgerCallId` + `attemptId` correlation key.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:268:The local ledger is append-only JSONL. One line represents one budget-relevant
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:269:LLM call attempt or refusal.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:271:The `usage` object records token counts using the full cache-aware token model.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:272:Provider-reported usage carries four first-class token fields:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:274:- `inputTokens`: the uncached remainder of the input only. This is NOT the total
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:275:  input. When prompt caching is active, the cached portion of the input is
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:276:  reported separately in `cacheReadInputTokens` (and, on the first write, in
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:277:  `cacheCreationInputTokens`); `inputTokens` is only the part of the input that
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:278:  was neither served from cache nor written to cache.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:279:- `outputTokens`: tokens generated by the model in the response.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:280:- `cacheCreationInputTokens`: input tokens written to the prompt cache on this
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:281:  call (cache writes cost more than base input).
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:282:- `cacheReadInputTokens`: input tokens served from the prompt cache on this call
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:283:  (cache reads cost a small fraction of base input).
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:285:This four-field shape matches prior art already in production: Managed Agents
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:286:(CMA) record exactly these four fields in
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:287:`span.model_request_end.model_usage`, so the ledger reuses the same shape rather
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:288:than inventing a new one. The real processed volume of a call is therefore
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:289:`inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens`,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:290:not `inputTokens + outputTokens` alone.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:292:Each record also carries a normalized canonical view and a raw provider digest
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:293:(see Multi-Provider Normalization below) so cross-source summaries stay
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:294:comparable without discarding provider fidelity.

docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:470:## Multi-Provider Normalization
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:472:Providers report usage with different field names and unit semantics. Two goals
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:473:are in tension: preserving provider-specific fidelity (so nothing is lost or
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:474:misinterpreted) and producing cross-source summaries (so usage across providers
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:476:provider-reported record, not one or the other:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:478:- `usage.raw`: the raw provider units and a provider usage `payloadDigest`,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:479:  preserving provider-specific meaning. The raw view is never discarded in favor
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:480:  of the canonical view; canonical is additive, not a replacement.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:481:- `usage.canonical`: a normalized canonical view with exactly four fields
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:482:  `{input, output, cacheCreation, cacheRead}`, matching the four-field token
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:483:  model. Cross-source summaries read the canonical view so providers are
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:486:Mapping rules (provider cache/cached-token fields to canonical cache fields):
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:488:- Each provider adapter must declare an explicit mapping from its reported usage
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:489:  fields to the canonical `{input, output, cacheCreation, cacheRead}` fields. The
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:490:  mapping must be explicit and reviewable, never implicit.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:491:- Anthropic-shaped providers map `input_tokens -> input`,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:492:  `output_tokens -> output`, `cache_creation_input_tokens -> cacheCreation`, and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:493:  `cache_read_input_tokens -> cacheRead`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:494:- Providers that report only a single "cached tokens" figure (cache reads, with
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:495:  no separate write count) map that figure to `cacheRead` and set
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:496:  `cacheCreation` according to what the provider actually reports; a value the
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:497:  provider does not report must not be inferred (see the provider-reported
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:498:  constraint on never inferring `0`).
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:499:- Providers that do not expose cache tokens at all set the canonical
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:500:  `cacheCreation` and `cacheRead` to `null` (and likewise the record's
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:501:  `cacheCreationInputTokens` / `cacheReadInputTokens`) rather than a silent `0`,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:502:  while still mapping `input` and `output`. The record stays
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:503:  `usage.source=provider-reported` because input/output are provider-reported;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:504:  per-dimension absence is expressed by setting those cache fields to `null`, not
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:505:  by `usage.source` (see the per-dimension absence rule under "Required record
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:506:  constraints"). For example, an OpenAI-style provider that reports only
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:507:  input/output emits `cacheCreationInputTokens: null` and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:508:  `cacheReadInputTokens: null` (canonical `cacheCreation: null`,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:510:- `canonical.input` follows the same uncached-remainder semantics as
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:511:  `inputTokens`: it is the uncached input only, not the gross input.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:515:Per-token prices change over time, and cache reads/writes are priced differently
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:516:from base input (cache reads cost roughly a small fraction of base input; cache
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:517:writes cost more than base input, with different multipliers for different cache
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:518:TTLs). A dollar amount baked into an append-only record therefore goes stale and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:519:becomes wrong the next time pricing changes, and an append-only record cannot be
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:520:corrected. Cost is consequently never stored as an absolute amount on the record.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:524:- Cost is derived only in a dedicated layer that pins `provider.model` plus a
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:525:  date to a versioned price table (per-model $/MTok plus cache-read and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:526:  cache-write multipliers). The four-field/canonical token counts feed that
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:527:  derivation.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:528:- The record carries a `pricingRef` / `pricingVersion` reference (a pointer to
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:529:  the versioned price-table snapshot in effect at `recordedAt`), not absolute
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:530:  prices. The price-table snapshot mechanism is what maps a `pricingRef` to the
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:531:  concrete per-model rates and cache multipliers.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:532:- No absolute dollar amount or hardcoded per-token price may be baked into the
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:533:  append-only record beyond the `pricingRef` reference. The append-only record
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:534:  stays a token-and-reference record; money is computed downstream.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:536:## Local Non-authority Boundary
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:538:The local ledger belongs to ordinary Proofbound workflow. It is a diagnostic and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:539:budget-accounting artifact, not Authority evidence.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:541:Local Non-authority rules:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:543:- Local ledger records must keep `authority.mode=local` or `shadow` unless a
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:544:  future explicit receipt-backed path writes a verified receipt reference.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:545:- Local records must keep `authority.receiptVerified=false`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:546:- Local records must not set `productionDone`, `authorityChanged`, or any
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:547:  equivalent Authority-completion flag.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:548:- Local prompt-size estimates must never become `receipt-backed-l2-plus`.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:549:- Host transcripts, local JSONL lines, dispatch receipts, and transport
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:550:  `accepted=true` responses must not be treated as signed Authority receipts.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:551:- Missing Authority configuration must not block ordinary local workflow unless
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:552:  a command is explicitly running in an Authority-required budget mode.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:554:## Authority Server Receipt-Backed Path
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:556:The future Authority Server path is separate from the local ledger path.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:560:- The execution plane submits a privacy-preserving usage evidence envelope to
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:562:- The Authority Server validates provider-reported usage, budget policy,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:563:  project/story/run binding, actor identity, and evidence adequacy.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:564:- The Authority Server signs an `AuthorityReceipt` or receipt proof that binds
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:565:  the ledger-relevant usage decision to the subject, digest, server key, and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:567:- Proofbound CLI may project that receipt into local status only after receipt
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:568:  signature verification and subject binding pass.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:569:- A local ledger line may include `authority.receiptId` only as a reference to a
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:570:  verified server receipt. The local line itself is not the receipt.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:572:Negative controls:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:574:- Transport acceptance without a signed receipt is not Authority usage proof.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:575:- A provider response with real token counts is not Authority proof by itself.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:576:- A local estimate is not Authority proof.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:577:- A local JSONL hash chain is not Authority proof.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:578:- A copied receipt id without signature verification and subject binding is not
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:579:  Authority proof.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:581:## Implementation Touchpoints
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:583:Future implementation should be split into narrow slices:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:585:1. Ledger schema and writer:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:586:   - define the JSONL schema and validators;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:587:   - write to `.lattice/usage/llm-usage.jsonl`;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:588:   - add the runtime artifact registry entry and gitignore behavior for that
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:589:     path;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:590:   - add a single append-only writer choke-point that all provider dispatch flows
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:591:     through (no second writer path; see Completeness Guarantee);
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:592:   - generate `ledgerCallId`, `attemptId`, `sequence`, and
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:593:     `supersedesRecordIds` before provider dispatch;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:594:   - reject raw prompt and transcript fields at runtime;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:595:   - include hash chaining for local tamper detection.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:596:2. Provider adapter extraction:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:597:   - map each provider's reported usage into the shared `provider-reported`
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:599:   - preserve provider-specific units in the raw view without normalizing away
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:601:     `{input, output, cacheCreation, cacheRead}` view (see Multi-Provider
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:602:     Normalization);
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:603:   - declare each provider's explicit cache/cached-token mapping into the
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:604:     canonical cache fields;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:605:   - attach final provider records to the locally generated call and attempt
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:606:     ids;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:607:   - record `unavailable` when provider usage is absent.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:608:3. Estimate path:
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:609:   - add preflight prompt-size estimate records for budget checks;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:610:   - prefer the provider `count_tokens` endpoint, fall back to a local tokenizer,
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:611:     then to a bytes/chars heuristic only when offline (see Estimate accuracy
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:612:     and fallback order);
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:613:   - label estimator name, version, unit, and confidence (`high | medium | low`),
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:614:     and bind the estimate to the exact `provider.model`;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:615:   - keep estimate records separate from final provider-reported records;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:616:   - mark estimate records superseded when a provider-reported final record or
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:617:     blocked refusal replaces them for summary accounting.
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:619:   - define local, shadow, and Authority-required budget modes;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:620:   - make over-budget preflight decisions fail closed before provider calls;
docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-llm-usage-ledger-execution-plan.md:621:   - make postflight provider-reported overages visible and auditable.

CLAUDE.md:376:## Worktree 生命周期
CLAUDE.md:378:每个 story 一个独立 worktree，互不干扰。这里的并行是 **本地 git worktree + 本地分支**，不是 GitHub/origin 分支；agent 不要创建或 push 远端 feature branch：
CLAUDE.md:380:1. `story_create` → 停在 **INIT**（在 main 分支上写 story 文件）
CLAUDE.md:381:2. `story_advance INIT_CHECK` → 自动创建 `.worktrees/B-xxx/`，分支 `story/B-xxx`
CLAUDE.md:382:3. **`cd .worktrees/B-xxx`**（必须切，否则 cwd 门禁拒绝）
CLAUDE.md:383:4. `story_advance PLAN` → 正式进入开发流程
CLAUDE.md:384:5. PLAN / DEV / TEST 全部在 worktree 里完成
CLAUDE.md:385:6. `story_advance --phase=TEST` → 推进 TEST
CLAUDE.md:386:7. `story_advance --phase=DONE` → 合并回本地 main 并清理 worktree（可从 worktree 子目录触发，清理目标仍是 git 顶层 worktree）；如果需要远端发布，只在本地 main 干净且已验证后，由人类显式运行 `lattice release_approve_push --confirm` 创建短 TTL 一次性 approval，再手动 `git push origin main`
CLAUDE.md:388:**cwd 门禁**：PLAN 起所有 `story_advance` 都校验 cwd 是 story 的 worktree。
CLAUDE.md:390:**远端写入纪律**：Lattice 的 story 分支是本地实现细节，用于隔离 worktree 和 DONE merge；不要把 `story/*`、`codex/*`、`lab/*` 等任务分支推到 GitHub。并行任务完成后的收束路径是本地 merge main + 清理 worktree，不是开远端 PR 分支。任何远端 publish 都默认被 `.githooks/pre-push` 拒绝；只有人类在干净本地 main 上运行 `lattice release_approve_push --confirm` 后，hook 才允许一次 exact `refs/heads/main` + exact SHA 的 `git push origin main`。
CLAUDE.md:392:**版本递增纪律**：每个会改变 Lattice CLI / runtime 行为的 story 合并回本地 `main` 后，必须把 CLI patch 版本递增 1（例如 `0.3.6` → `0.3.7`），同步 `package.json` / lockfile / `LATTICE_CLI_VERSION`，运行 `npm --prefix packages/main run build`，并确认 `lattice --version` 输出新版本。纯文档、story metadata-only、review evidence-only 合并不强制 bump，避免无意义消耗版本号。
CLAUDE.md:394:**Host DONE convergence / drift handling（DONE 收束纪律）**：并行 story 收束时按此操作，避免在 DONE 前反复撞。这是对既有机制的**投影**，规则源以下列决策文档为准、不在此重定义：`docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md`、`docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md`、`docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-automation-execution-plan.md`、`docs/requirements/decisions/review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md`，以及 `lattice done_prepare --help`。
CLAUDE.md:396:1. **TEST→DONE 先 done_prepare，不要直接撞 `story_advance DONE`**：先运行 `lattice done_prepare --storyId=B-xxxx --mergeMain --refreshStale --validate`（会 merge main、安全 refresh stale evidence、validate，并聚合下一步 blocker）；只有 `DONE prepare: PASS` 后再 `lattice story_advance --phase=DONE`。
CLAUDE.md:397:2. **Host 不自判 freshness**：读 `done_prepare` / freshness-reader 的分类结果，不要拿原始 hash 自己判 pass。
CLAUDE.md:398:3. **headHash-only drift** 通常是 metadata / provenance 移动，**不是**强重跑信号。
CLAUDE.md:399:4. **materialHash-only drift + storyFilesHash 不变**：unrelated whole-tree drift 候选（以下为当前 warn/advisory 投影，enforce 模式落地后可能收紧）：
CLAUDE.md:400:   > materialHash-only drift with unchanged storyFilesHash is usually unrelated whole-tree drift. In current warn/advisory paths, Lattice may downgrade this to re-attestation advisory instead of forcing full re-review/quorum. Host must follow done_prepare / freshness-reader output, not self-classify it as pass.
CLAUDE.md:401:5. **storyFilesHash drift** 才是 story-owned material drift 的**强信号**：review pass / quorum / delivery 可能需要重新绑定（消费方不同：reviewer-pass 严格，floor / escalation / delivery-check 在 storyFilesHash 不变时降级接受）。
CLAUDE.md:402:6. **done_prepare 不是万能豁免**：它能自动化 merge / refresh / validate / next-action，但**跳不过 related drift**——若 merge main 改到了当前 story-owned files（storyFilesHash 真变），仍需重 review / 重 quorum / 重 delivery。
CLAUDE.md:403:7. **metadata-only dirty** 的处理：
CLAUDE.md:404:   > Metadata-only dirty handling is governed by done_prepare/lifecycle_check; see B-9dfb once merged. Host must not manually bypass cleanTree.

CLAUDE.md:409:⚠ worktree 缺 node_modules: worktree 根
CLAUDE.md:410:  缺依赖会导致 tsc / lattice validate 解析不到模块而失败。
CLAUDE.md:411:  → 补救（推荐）：cd <worktree> && npm install

CLAUDE.md:839:### REVIEW→TEST gate behavior (`canPassReviewGuard`) + incremental review context (B-f675)
CLAUDE.md:841:The structured `canPassReviewGuard` gate (`core/machine.ts`, consumed by the REVIEW→TEST transition) decides on reviewer evidence + findings, NOT on free text. Its accurate semantics:
CLAUDE.md:843:- **An invalid (stale / unknown-run / tampered) current-round binding blocks in ALL rounds.** `collectReviewerEvidenceState` validates every reviewer finding / review-pass against its bound `reviewRunId` (signature, lane, current round, fresh head/material hash, scope binding; plus — for an open FINDING only — the lane's current-latest run, since a PASS is accepted on any current-round fresh run). If any current-round reviewer evidence is invalid, the gate fails closed BEFORE the round split — round 1 and round 2+ alike.
CLAUDE.md:844:- **Round 1 (`roundCount <= 1`): requires EVERY opt-in reviewer to have a valid current-round verdict, plus quorum.** The opt-in set is the same one `lattice reviewer_list` reports (baseline concept + quality + test-coverage, plus behavior/docs by riskSignals / `.md` touchpoints). Missing any opt-in reviewer, or failing the quorum check, blocks.
CLAUDE.md:845:- **Round 2+ (`roundCount >= 2`): requires only `>= 1` valid current-round receipt** (finding or review-pass). The framework still skips no reviewer; this only relaxes the gate's minimum, not the reviewer roster.
CLAUDE.md:846:- **A verified open blocking finding blocks** (after round decay): `status=open` AND severity in the round's effective blocking set (round 1 = profile `blockingSeverities`; round 2 = critical+high; round 3+ = critical) AND `evidenceState` verified-or-missing. `suspected` / `disproven` never block.
CLAUDE.md:848:**`lattice review_incremental_context --storyId=B-xxx --role=<reviewer>`** is a strictly read-only advisory: it returns the reviewer's prior verdict, the `headHash` that verdict was bound to, and the MATERIAL files changed since (rename-aware `git diff --name-status -M`, so a renamed file still counts as changed), plus `scopeChanged` / `isFirstPass`. A first-timer (no prior pass) gets `isFirstPass=true` and the full `main...HEAD` material diff. **It writes nothing and changes none of the gate inputs above** (findings / review-passes / review-runs / currentReviewRound); calling it does not alter `canPassReviewGuard` (proven by `test:review-incremental-context-smoke`).
CLAUDE.md:850:`isFirstPass=true` is the authoritative "no usable incremental baseline" signal and covers TWO sub-cases: (a) the reviewer never passed before, AND (b) a prior verdict exists but the run it was bound to has an unresolvable `headHash`. In sub-case (b) `priorVerdict` is non-null (informational) while `priorHeadHash` is null and `changedFiles` is the full `main...HEAD` diff — so a JSON consumer must key off `isFirstPass` (not `priorVerdict`) to decide whether an incremental baseline exists. Likewise `scopeChanged` is forced to true whenever `isFirstPass=true`, so it may be true even when `changedFiles` is empty; only when `isFirstPass=false` does `scopeChanged === (changedFiles.length > 0)`.
CLAUDE.md:852:**Round 2+ informed targeted re-review (operator judgement):** because the round-2+ gate needs only `>= 1` valid current-round receipt, when entering REVIEW for round >= 2 the next-step output appends an advisory listing the active reviewers whose scope changed since their last pass. An operator MAY then re-run only those scope-changed reviewers (`lattice review_incremental_context --role=<name>` to inspect each), rather than re-running the entire roster. This is your call — the framework skips nobody and the gate is unchanged; it is purely an operator efficiency hint.

CLAUDE.md:955:## 合并态组合审查（流程框架并行 story）
CLAUDE.md:957:单 story REVIEW 只看单个 story 的 diff，看不到「两个各自局部正确的 story 叠加成全局漏洞」的跨 story 交互。**当多个流程框架类 story（触及 dirty/状态 classifier、gate policy、命令入口门禁、auto-commit、DONE merge 语义任一）并行合并到 main 时**，合并后应对 main 的合并态做一次只读 combination review，逐项过分类优先级顺序 / gate policy 表 / 命令入口门禁 / auto-commit-dirty 交互 / DONE merge 语义。普通业务 story 不触发。这是 advisory 流程纪律，不是 CLI gate。规则来自 B-8db9 incident（B-cf60 + B-4b22 各自单 story review 通过、合并 main 后叠加成 CRITICAL gate 绕过）。

CLAUDE.md:1001:## pre-push hook + 递归 tsc gate
CLAUDE.md:1003:B-5a28 针对「Lattice 自举开发」场景引入两条防线：(1) `lattice validate --lint` 递归扫 monorepo 所有子包 tsconfig，(2) `.githooks/pre-push` 作为独立于 Lattice CLI 自身的外部 gate。B-eab3 补齐了第二条（hook 之前只配了 `core.hooksPath` 却没创建文件，全部 git hook 静默失效）。本段记录 hook 的完整行为与启用方式。
CLAUDE.md:1008:git config core.hooksPath .githooks
CLAUDE.md:1011:`.githooks/pre-push` 跟仓库一起提交，启用后每次 `git push` 前先默认拒绝远端写入；非 `main` 的远端分支 push 直接拒绝，`main` push 也必须携带 `lattice release_approve_push --confirm` 写入的短 TTL 一次性 approval，匹配后才继续跑递归 tsc gate。
CLAUDE.md:1015:pre-push hook 的核心设计约束：**不调用旧 CLI alias**。原因：hook 要防御的是全局 CLI 可执行文件版本错位情形；若 hook 自己依赖可能过期的全局入口，它就会跟着翻车（B-9bd9 假 DONE 的根因之一）。实现只用 `git` / `find` / `node` / `npx tsc` / `npm run build`，完全绕开全局 CLI 版本（`node` 仅用于解析 `package.json` 的 `name` 字段做自举仓检测，不调旧入口）。
CLAUDE.md:1019:`.githooks/pre-push`（跟仓库一起提交，便于跨 clone 复用）逐步行为：
CLAUDE.md:1021:- 临时文件用 `mktemp -d` 创建唯一临时目录，`trap '... cleanup' EXIT` 在 hook 退出时清理（避免并发 push 同名互覆盖、`/tmp` 累积）。`mktemp` 失败 → push 被拒
CLAUDE.md:1022:- 先 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` 拿 REPO_ROOT
CLAUDE.md:1023:- **远端写入纪律**：读取 pre-push stdin 的 ref update；任何非 `refs/heads/main` 的 `refs/heads/*` 直接拒绝。`refs/heads/main` 也默认拒绝，除非 `.lattice/tmp/remote-push-approval.json` 的 schema / remote / branch / exact SHA / TTL 全匹配；匹配后 hook 会消费该 one-shot approval。Lattice 并行开发只使用本地 worktree/local branch，完成后合回本地 main、清理 worktree，并停止在本地。
CLAUDE.md:1024:- **Lattice 自举仓检测**：
CLAUDE.md:1025:  1. `$REPO_ROOT/packages/main/package.json` 文件存在——不存在则非 Lattice 仓，立即 `exit 0`（对非 Lattice 仓零摩擦）
CLAUDE.md:1026:  2. **`node` 可用性检测**：用 `command -v node` 探测。`node` 缺失时 **fail-closed**——无法判断本仓是否 Lattice 自举仓，向 stderr 打印明确警告并 `exit 1` 拒绝 push（不静默 `exit 0`，否则 tsc gate 会被无声绕过）
CLAUDE.md:1027:  3. 用 `node` 解析 package.json 的 `name` 字段，为 `@lattice/core` 才继续；否则非 Lattice 自身，立即 `exit 0`
CLAUDE.md:1028:  注意本仓是扁平布局 `packages/main`，不是嵌套布局
CLAUDE.md:1029:- **先构建 `packages/main`**：`npm --prefix packages/main run build`。原因是 `packages/utils` 的源码 import `packages/main/dist` 的编译产物，若 `dist` 不存在，递归 tsc 跑到 `packages/utils` 会因找不到模块而 FAIL。`npm run build` 即 tsc（非 Lattice CLI 命令，符合约束）。构建失败 → push 被拒
CLAUDE.md:1030:- **递归 tsc**：`find` REPO_ROOT 下所有 `tsconfig.json`（排除黑名单目录 `node_modules / dist / build / .worktrees / .git`），对每个所在目录跑 `npx tsc --noEmit -p <dir>`。覆盖面与 `validate --lint` 递归扫子包对齐，消除 B-9bd9 的单根 tsconfig 子包盲区
CLAUDE.md:1035:`packages/main/src/handlers/validate-lint.ts`：
CLAUDE.md:1037:- `TSCONFIG_IGNORE_DIRS: ReadonlySet<string>` — 模块级常量黑名单（`node_modules / dist / build / .worktrees / .git`）。**扩展忽略目录需修改该常量本身**，不走函数参数。
CLAUDE.md:1038:- `findTsconfigs(projectRoot, deps?: { readdir?, stat?, fileExists? })` — BFS 扫目录，命中黑名单的子目录剪枝；返回所有 `tsconfig.json` 绝对路径。第二参是**依赖注入接口**（测试用，替换 fs helpers），**不是 options 也没有 `ignoreDirs` 参数**——黑名单由 TSCONFIG_IGNORE_DIRS 常量固定。默认 stat 用 `lstatSync` 且跳过 symlink，防 npm link 场景下节点指回仓库根触发无限递归（F-005）。
CLAUDE.md:1039:- 每个 tsconfig 逐个 `tsc --noEmit -p <dir>`，任一 fail → 整体 fail + 合并所有 stderr。工具缺失判定用显式 `passes` 计数：仅在「从未成功跑过任何 tsc 且从未有 fail」时才视为 skipped；已有 pass 后再遇 toolMissing 当 fail 记录，别静默吞掉前面的 pass（F-007 / F-014）。
CLAUDE.md:1041:**改动前的 bug**：老实现 hardcode `<projectRoot>/tsconfig.json` 单根，avalon 根没有 tsconfig.json → tsc gate 永远 skip → 子包编译错误永远漏检（B-9bd9 翻车根因）。
CLAUDE.md:1045:`tests/validate-lint.test.ts` 用 `CommandRunner` 类型依赖注入，**不 spawn 真 tsc**。签名：
CLAUDE.md:1048:type CommandRunner = (cmd: string, args: string[], cwd: string) => {
CLAUDE.md:1049:  code: number;           // 进程退出码；spawn 失败时为 -1
CLAUDE.md:1050:  output: string;         // stdout + stderr 合并后的纯字符串（不区分流）
CLAUDE.md:1051:  spawnError: boolean;    // true = 可执行文件缺失（ENOENT），调用方应视为 skipped
CLAUDE.md:1055:- `output` 是 stdout / stderr 合并后的单字符串，不是两个独立字段——业务只需「tsc 说了啥」一坨文本，合并简化断言
CLAUDE.md:1056:- `spawnError` 区分「二进制不存在（npx / tsc 没装）」与「二进制可跑但编译失败（exit code != 0）」两种不同语义：前者 skipped，后者 fail
CLAUDE.md:1057:- 测 `findTsconfigs` 的黑名单剪枝逻辑用 fixture 目录树
CLAUDE.md:1058:- 测 `runTsc` / `runLint` 的聚合行为用 stub runner 注入预设返回（模拟成功 / 失败 / 混合 / 工具缺失）
CLAUDE.md:1061:生产路径用 `defaultRunner`（`child_process.spawnSync` + 合并 stdout/stderr + 区分 ENOENT）。
CLAUDE.md:1063:### 与 CLI gate 的关系
CLAUDE.md:1065:`lattice validate --lint` 是 REVIEW→TEST preflight 的 CLI gate 之一（见上文「CLI gate」段）。B-5a28 前：lint gate 只扫根 tsconfig → monorepo 子包漏检。B-5a28 后：lint gate 递归扫所有子包 → 子包编译错误直接 block REVIEW→TEST。pre-push hook 是「即使 lint gate 被跳过也兜住」的最后一道防线。
CLAUDE.md:1067:see story/B-5a28
CLAUDE.md:1071:- 所有 Story 操作通过 `lattice` CLI 完成
CLAUDE.md:1072:- 测试统一通过 `lattice validate` 执行
CLAUDE.md:1073:- `lattice validate` 全绿 = 可以提交
CLAUDE.md:1074:- 调用出错时先 `lattice <command> --help`，不要靠记忆猜参数

docs/host-run-usage.md:6:until a terminal record exists. A caller may attach, time out, disconnect, or
docs/host-run-usage.md:7:return after 30 seconds without cancelling or replacing the provider run.
docs/host-run-usage.md:9:The same launch path records optional LLM usage diagnostics. Usage rows are not

docs/host-run-usage.md:11:admission. `lattice usage_sweep` remains the read-only companion for sessions

docs/host-run-usage.md:18:desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every
docs/host-run-usage.md:19:`host_run` receives a durable `runId`, an absolute deadline and an exclusive

docs/host-run-usage.md:27:Usage rows are diagnostics only (`gateEvidence=false`). They never gate the

docs/host-run-usage.md:31:## `host_run`
docs/host-run-usage.md:34:lattice host_run --host <codex|claude> --agentType <type> \
docs/host-run-usage.md:35:  [--storyId B-xxxx] [--phase DEV] \
docs/host-run-usage.md:36:  ( --prompt "<text>" | --promptFile <path> ) \
docs/host-run-usage.md:37:  [--reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-001] [--lane <reviewer-lane>] \
docs/host-run-usage.md:38:  [--timeoutMs <ms>] [--deadlineMs <ms>] [--detach] \
docs/host-run-usage.md:42:`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with
docs/host-run-usage.md:43:`runId/state/generation/deadlineAt`. Foreground mode submits the same durable
docs/host-run-usage.md:44:run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:
docs/host-run-usage.md:47:lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":4,"afterSequence":12,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
docs/host-run-usage.md:48:lattice host_run_cancel '{"runId":"<runId>","reason":"operator cancelled"}'
docs/host-run-usage.md:51:`waitMs` is capped at 30 seconds. A bounded return means “wake the caller and
docs/host-run-usage.md:52:inspect the current snapshot”, not “the provider failed”. Completion is known
docs/host-run-usage.md:53:only from `state=completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out` plus the terminal
docs/host-run-usage.md:54:receipt. Provider-output silence and a stale output timestamp are diagnostics,
docs/host-run-usage.md:55:never terminal predicates and never automatic-restart authorization. The
docs/host-run-usage.md:56:absolute deadline prevents permanent waiting; the next status/cancel/attach
docs/host-run-usage.md:57:touch reconciles an overdue run to terminal truth and records whether process
docs/host-run-usage.md:58:cleanup made replacement safe.
docs/host-run-usage.md:60:The host subprocess executes in the **resolved project root** (the `--root`
docs/host-run-usage.md:61:target — the same root the usage-ledger rows are attributed to), independent of
docs/host-run-usage.md:62:the caller's current working directory, so where the host actually runs can
docs/host-run-usage.md:63:never diverge from where the ledger says it ran.
docs/host-run-usage.md:65:Provider output is durably journaled and projected to an attached foreground
docs/host-run-usage.md:66:caller as it arrives. Worker heartbeat and `lastProviderProgressAt` are separate:
docs/host-run-usage.md:67:the former proves only that the supervisor can update state; the latter moves
docs/host-run-usage.md:68:only when observable provider bytes arrive. `providerProgressMode=unobservable`
docs/host-run-usage.md:69:is reported honestly when progress cannot be observed. A one-line usage summary
docs/host-run-usage.md:70:is written to stderr, for example:
docs/host-run-usage.md:73:usage recorded: provider=openai input=10202 cacheRead=11008 output=85 (recordId llmuse_...)
docs/host-run-usage.md:76:Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
docs/host-run-usage.md:77:usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
docs/host-run-usage.md:78:capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
docs/host-run-usage.md:79:flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
docs/host-run-usage.md:80:poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
docs/host-run-usage.md:81:happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
docs/host-run-usage.md:82:retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
docs/host-run-usage.md:83:usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
docs/host-run-usage.md:84:rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
docs/host-run-usage.md:85:valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
docs/host-run-usage.md:86:later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
docs/host-run-usage.md:87:(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
docs/host-run-usage.md:88:perfectly good final usage event).
docs/host-run-usage.md:90:### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)
docs/host-run-usage.md:92:| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
docs/host-run-usage.md:94:| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
docs/host-run-usage.md:95:| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |
docs/host-run-usage.md:97:In `--json` mode the full host transcript is delivered live on **stderr** so that
docs/host-run-usage.md:98:**stdout stays clean** for the one JSON result; the JSON `stdout` field therefore
docs/host-run-usage.md:99:carries only the bounded usage-parse tail, not the full transcript.
docs/host-run-usage.md:101:If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
docs/host-run-usage.md:102:but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
docs/host-run-usage.md:103:`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
docs/host-run-usage.md:104:`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
docs/host-run-usage.md:105:downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
docs/host-run-usage.md:106:delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
docs/host-run-usage.md:107:event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async
docs/host-run-usage.md:108:stream error too. `host_run` attaches (and, in a `finally`, removes) its own
docs/host-run-usage.md:109:stdout/stderr `'error'` listeners for the duration of the run, so a real EPIPE is
docs/host-run-usage.md:110:contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
docs/host-run-usage.md:111:once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are
docs/host-run-usage.md:112:skipped rather than risk a late unhandled `'error'`, and **every** live
docs/host-run-usage.md:113:passthrough chunk write *and* final diagnostic write is settle-aware:
docs/host-run-usage.md:114:outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
docs/host-run-usage.md:115:serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
docs/host-run-usage.md:116:by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
docs/host-run-usage.md:117:command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
docs/host-run-usage.md:118:from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
docs/host-run-usage.md:119:fires while a listener is attached.
docs/host-run-usage.md:121:Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
docs/host-run-usage.md:122:runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
docs/host-run-usage.md:123:forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
docs/host-run-usage.md:124:non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
docs/host-run-usage.md:125:`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.
docs/host-run-usage.md:129:Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
docs/host-run-usage.md:130:when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
docs/host-run-usage.md:131:registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
docs/host-run-usage.md:132:lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
docs/host-run-usage.md:133:identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
docs/host-run-usage.md:134:registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
docs/host-run-usage.md:135:in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
docs/host-run-usage.md:136:attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
docs/host-run-usage.md:137:process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.
docs/host-run-usage.md:139:An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
docs/host-run-usage.md:140:`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
docs/host-run-usage.md:141:review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
docs/host-run-usage.md:142:the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
docs/host-run-usage.md:143:direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
docs/host-run-usage.md:144:below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
docs/host-run-usage.md:145:capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
docs/host-run-usage.md:146:registered broker set.
docs/host-run-usage.md:148:The attestation nonce is atomically consumed once to prevent replay. That local
docs/host-run-usage.md:150:ancestry is corroboration rather than required authority: an unavailable `ps`
docs/host-run-usage.md:151:view does not reject a valid broker attestation, but any observable mixed
docs/host-run-usage.md:152:Codex/Claude ancestry rejects direct evidence even when the nearest provider
docs/host-run-usage.md:153:matches. A same-UID/root attacker that can replace trusted configuration or
docs/host-run-usage.md:154:instrument the broker is outside this local assurance boundary.

docs/host-run-usage.md:223:The current agy print CLI accepts prompt bytes only as a plaintext argv value.
docs/host-run-usage.md:224:Managed `host_run --host agy` therefore refuses before provider spawn until agy
docs/host-run-usage.md:225:provides stdin or a protected prompt-file transport; Proofbound will not trade
