docs/host-run-usage.md:230:Every usage row carries the attribution passed to `host_run`:
docs/host-run-usage.md:232:| Argument | Ledger field | Notes |
docs/host-run-usage.md:234:| `--storyId` | `storyId` | Canonical Story id. Omit for an adhoc run. |
docs/host-run-usage.md:235:| `--agentType` | `agentType` | e.g. `reviewer`, `autopilot-repair`, `host-readiness-probe`. Required. |
docs/host-run-usage.md:236:| `--phase` | `phase` | When omitted and `--storyId` is set, the phase resolves from the **configured story store** at call time (honoring a project's `storyDir`); an explicit `--phase` is used as-is and the store is never read. |
docs/host-run-usage.md:237:| `--reviewRunId` | `threadId` | e.g. `B-xxxx:RR-001`. Joins rows against `review-runs.json`. |
docs/host-run-usage.md:238:| `--lane` | `subagentId` | e.g. `lattice-review-quality`. |
docs/host-run-usage.md:240:`--reviewRunId` must start with `<storyId>:` when `--storyId` is given, so a
docs/host-run-usage.md:241:ledger row can never silently mis-join across stories — a mismatch is refused
docs/host-run-usage.md:242:before any host is spawned. Omitting `--reviewRunId` / `--lane` leaves
docs/host-run-usage.md:243:`threadId` / `subagentId` null (no empty-string pollution).
docs/host-run-usage.md:245:When `--storyId` is given **without** `--phase`, the phase is resolved through the
docs/host-run-usage.md:246:configured story store; a story unknown to that store is refused pre-spawn. When
docs/host-run-usage.md:247:`--phase` is supplied the store is never consulted, so `--phase` works with or
docs/host-run-usage.md:248:without `--storyId` even in a project whose story metadata lives under a
docs/host-run-usage.md:249:custom `storyDir`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:251:## Per-host usage semantics
docs/host-run-usage.md:253:Provider truth is preferred over estimates; an absence is recorded as an explicit
docs/host-run-usage.md:254:`source=unavailable`, never a fabricated zero.
docs/host-run-usage.md:256:- **codex** — parses the terminal `turn.completed` usage event from
docs/host-run-usage.md:257:  `codex exec --json` and maps it to `{ input: input_tokens - cached_input_tokens,
docs/host-run-usage.md:258:  cacheRead: cached_input_tokens, cacheCreation: null, output: output_tokens }`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:259:  The `input` field is the **uncached remainder** (codex `input_tokens` includes
docs/host-run-usage.md:260:  cached input); the original payload (including `reasoning_output_tokens`) is
docs/host-run-usage.md:261:  digested raw.
docs/host-run-usage.md:262:- **claude** — parses the stream-json `result` envelope usage via
docs/host-run-usage.md:263:  `parseClaudeCliOutput` (the four-field Anthropic usage plus the served model).
docs/host-run-usage.md:264:- **agy** — recorded as `source=unavailable` with provider `antigravity` and an
docs/host-run-usage.md:265:  explicit `unavailableReason`. agy print mode exposes no usage surface
docs/host-run-usage.md:266:  (verified 2026-07-10), so no counts can be reported.
docs/host-run-usage.md:268:A parse miss (no `turn.completed` event, no `result` usage) records an
docs/host-run-usage.md:269:`unavailable` final with a reason rather than inventing counts.
docs/host-run-usage.md:271:同样的诚实口径适用于 reviewer A/B：缺少 exact per-role historical envelope、
docs/host-run-usage.md:272:reviewer output、adjudication bytes 或 provider receipt 时结果是
docs/host-run-usage.md:273:`INCONCLUSIVE`，不是“0 token”或已证明的节省。B-235e 的独立 replay campaign
docs/host-run-usage.md:276:The one-line usage summary reflects the **actual append outcome**, not merely
docs/host-run-usage.md:277:that the provider envelope parsed. When the ledger append itself fails (a corrupt
docs/host-run-usage.md:278:ledger, or a lock-wait timeout that skips the write), the summary reports a
docs/host-run-usage.md:279:skipped state (`recorded: none`, reason `ledger_append_failed(...)`) and the
docs/host-run-usage.md:280:stderr line reads `usage: ledger_append_failed(...)` — it never claims
docs/host-run-usage.md:281:`usage recorded` for a row that never landed. This applies to all three hosts;
docs/host-run-usage.md:282:the provider is still surfaced for attribution, but token counts stay null. A
docs/host-run-usage.md:283:provider record that BUILT fine but whose append failed is reported as an
docs/host-run-usage.md:284:append failure keyed on the parsed usage — it is **never degraded to
docs/host-run-usage.md:285:`source=unavailable`** (which would falsely read as "the provider reported
docs/host-run-usage.md:286:nothing"), and no second `unavailable` final is attempted for it.
docs/host-run-usage.md:288:The same honesty gate covers the **blocked rows**: a cap refusal claims
docs/host-run-usage.md:289:`recorded: blocked` (and, for a concurrency refusal, surfaces the blocked row's
docs/host-run-usage.md:290:`recordId`) only when the blocked row **actually appended**. When that append is
docs/host-run-usage.md:291:swallowed too, the refusal itself is unchanged — still fail-closed, no spawn,
docs/host-run-usage.md:292:non-zero exit — but the summary reports `recorded: none` with `recordId: null`
docs/host-run-usage.md:293:and a composed reason that keeps the refusal visible, e.g.
docs/host-run-usage.md:294:`hard_budget_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)` or
docs/host-run-usage.md:295:`concurrency_cap_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)`. A recordId is never
docs/host-run-usage.md:296:minted for a blocked row that never persisted.
docs/host-run-usage.md:298:## Caps (fail-closed, before spawn)
docs/host-run-usage.md:300:With the usage ledger enabled, both caps run at the choke point BEFORE a host
docs/host-run-usage.md:301:is spawned, and each refusal attempts to record a
docs/host-run-usage.md:302:`decision.kind=blocked` ledger row (diagnostics-honest; an append failure is
docs/host-run-usage.md:303:reported as `recorded: none`). With `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0`, budget enforcement
docs/host-run-usage.md:304:and every ledger row are disabled; the provider-process capacity admission
docs/host-run-usage.md:305:still runs before every spawn and refuses fail-closed without claiming a
docs/host-run-usage.md:306:blocked row was persisted.
docs/host-run-usage.md:308:- **Per-dispatch hard budget** — reuses the existing `LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS`
docs/host-run-usage.md:309:  preflight guard per call. An over-budget preflight estimate refuses with
docs/host-run-usage.md:310:  `reasonCode hard_budget_exceeded` before spawning.
docs/host-run-usage.md:311:- **Provider-process concurrency** — a shared slot registry under
docs/host-run-usage.md:312:  `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/`
docs/host-run-usage.md:313:  holds **fixed numbered slots** `slot-0.json` .. `slot-(cap-1).json`, one per
docs/host-run-usage.md:314:  live run (pid + `startedAt` + an acquire-minted **ownership token**).
docs/host-run-usage.md:315:  Admission and reclaim are serialized by the ownership-checked provider
docs/host-run-usage.md:316:  registry lock, then the selected fixed slot is created with exclusive `wx`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:317:  The lock makes the live-count check, stale reclaim, cap-lowering check and
docs/host-run-usage.md:318:  create one cross-process transaction, so simultaneous starts and corrupt-slot
docs/host-run-usage.md:319:  replacement cannot slip past the cap. When every index
docs/host-run-usage.md:320:  under `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default **4**; unset / invalid /
docs/host-run-usage.md:321:  `<=0` falls back to the default; an explicit larger value is honored) is
docs/host-run-usage.md:322:  held, the run refuses fail-closed with a non-zero exit, prints the live-run
docs/host-run-usage.md:323:  list, and, when the ledger is enabled, writes a blocked row with `reasonCode
docs/host-run-usage.md:324:  concurrency_cap_exceeded`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:325:  Slot reclaim is **ownership-aware** (mirroring the ledger-lock doctrine
docs/host-run-usage.md:326:  below): a slot with a recorded **dead pid** is reclaimed at any age; a slot
docs/host-run-usage.md:327:  whose metadata is **missing/corrupt** (the holder crashed between creating
docs/host-run-usage.md:328:  the file and its metadata landing) is reclaimed once its mtime exceeds the
docs/host-run-usage.md:329:  `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_SLOT_STALE_MS` orphan backstop (default **6h**); a slot
docs/host-run-usage.md:330:  with a **live** recorded pid is **never reclaimed by age** — a long host run
docs/host-run-usage.md:331:  keeps its admission and waiters refuse at cap. Reclaim re-verifies the
docs/host-run-usage.md:332:  occupant immediately before the unlink under the same registry lock and then
docs/host-run-usage.md:333:  re-creates exclusively, so a crashed run never wedges the cap and a racing
docs/host-run-usage.md:334:  reclaimer cannot delete a slot a new holder just re-acquired. Slot release on
docs/host-run-usage.md:335:  exit is best-effort, registry-serialized and **token-guarded**:
docs/host-run-usage.md:336:  the file is unlinked only while it still carries the releasing run's own
docs/host-run-usage.md:337:  token, so a reclaimed-and-re-acquired slot survives the original holder's
docs/host-run-usage.md:338:  late release. Raising the cap mid-flight exposes more indexes; lowering it
docs/host-run-usage.md:339:  counts every live high-index slot and refuses new starts until the total live
docs/host-run-usage.md:340:  count drops below the new cap.
docs/host-run-usage.md:342:Blocked rows are provider-honest: a refusal records the provider of the host
docs/host-run-usage.md:343:that was asked to run (`openai` for codex, `anthropic` for claude,
docs/host-run-usage.md:344:`antigravity` for agy), never a hard-coded default.
docs/host-run-usage.md:346:The autopilot Claude repair launch (`lattice autopilot execute
docs/host-run-usage.md:347:--allowClaudeRepair`) passes the **same pre-spawn admission** in both ledger
docs/host-run-usage.md:348:modes. With the ledger ON, budget and capacity refusals can also write the
docs/host-run-usage.md:349:diagnostic blocked row. With the ledger OFF there are no usage rows or budget
docs/host-run-usage.md:350:guard, but capacity admission remains mandatory and the slot is still released
docs/host-run-usage.md:351:after the run.
docs/host-run-usage.md:353:The `cross_host_review` Codex leaf runs through ManagedHostRun and the same
docs/host-run-usage.md:354:provider admission (provider `openai`). It supports detach/resume by exact
docs/host-run-usage.md:355:`managedRunId`, never spawns a replacement on resume, and binds the terminal
docs/host-run-usage.md:356:`receiptId` into host-B verdict provenance. Budget/cap/provider failures still
docs/host-run-usage.md:357:produce an honest blocked/error decision; raw stdout is never gate evidence.
docs/host-run-usage.md:359:Concurrent runs' ledger appends are serialized by a cross-process lock at the
docs/host-run-usage.md:360:writer choke point (an atomic `llm-usage.jsonl.lock/` directory with a bounded
docs/host-run-usage.md:361:wait), so parallel host runs can never interleave appends and break the ledger
docs/host-run-usage.md:362:hash chain — a writer that cannot acquire the lock in time skips its append
docs/host-run-usage.md:363:(an honest under-count) rather than corrupting the chain. Lock reclaim is
docs/host-run-usage.md:364:ownership-aware: the acquirer records `owner.json` (holder pid + a unique
docs/host-run-usage.md:365:release token) inside the lock dir, and a held lock is reclaimed only when
docs/host-run-usage.md:366:that pid is dead, or — for an ownerless/corrupt lock, i.e. the holder crashed
docs/host-run-usage.md:367:between creating the dir and recording ownership — when the dir mtime exceeds
docs/host-run-usage.md:368:the `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_MS` orphan backstop. A live holder is
docs/host-run-usage.md:369:never reclaimed no matter how long it holds the lock (slow filesystem, GC
docs/host-run-usage.md:370:pause, suspension); release removes the lock only while `owner.json` still
docs/host-run-usage.md:371:carries the releaser's own token.
docs/host-run-usage.md:373:There is **no queuing** in this story: over the cap means refuse, not wait.
docs/host-run-usage.md:375:Set `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0` to disable usage preflight/budget/final rows. It
docs/host-run-usage.md:376:does **not** disable ManagedHostRun ownership or provider-process admission.
docs/host-run-usage.md:378:## Diagnostics, cleanup, and trust boundary
docs/host-run-usage.md:380:`lattice doctor --full` lists every managed run with state, worker liveness,
docs/host-run-usage.md:381:worker heartbeat, provider progress mode/time, deadline, cancellation,
docs/host-run-usage.md:382:residual-process status, `replacementSafe`, and retention state. `lattice
docs/host-run-usage.md:383:doctor --repair` removes heavy terminal run directories only after the 90-day
docs/host-run-usage.md:384:retention window and first archives the sealed minimal receipt plus imported
docs/host-run-usage.md:385:evidence-binding digest under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. Active or
docs/host-run-usage.md:386:corrupt runs and any directory still carrying one-shot inputs are retained
docs/host-run-usage.md:387:fail-closed for inspection; failed launch/claim paths erase prompt, capability,
docs/host-run-usage.md:388:and one-shot environment immediately. Per-run live output is capped at 8 MiB;
docs/host-run-usage.md:389:status readers page bounded frames and surface truncation rather than loading an
docs/host-run-usage.md:392:The runtime directory is local and mode 0700; sensitive one-shot files are 0600.
docs/host-run-usage.md:393:This protects against other users under ordinary filesystem permissions, not a
docs/host-run-usage.md:394:same-UID/root attacker. Operators must treat retained live output as locally
docs/host-run-usage.md:395:sensitive. Native Codex/Claude subagent APIs are deliberately out of scope:
docs/host-run-usage.md:396:ManagedHostRun owns only cross-provider CLI processes launched by Proofbound.
docs/host-run-usage.md:398:## `usage_sweep` (read-only retro-attribution)
docs/host-run-usage.md:401:lattice usage_sweep --since 2026-07-01 [--json]
docs/host-run-usage.md:404:`usage_sweep` stream-reads `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and
docs/host-run-usage.md:405:`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` since a cutoff and reports per-session token
docs/host-run-usage.md:406:totals, originator (desktop vs exec vs claude-code), cwd, first/last timestamps,
docs/host-run-usage.md:407:and `B-xxxx` story mentions, plus a per-story rollup and grand totals. It exists
docs/host-run-usage.md:408:to make runs that never went through `host_run` (interactive desktop sessions in
docs/host-run-usage.md:409:particular) at least visible.
docs/host-run-usage.md:411:- The report header states **NON-AUTHORITATIVE ESTIMATE** prominently in both
docs/host-run-usage.md:412:  the human table and `--json`. The totals come from host transcript stores, not
docs/host-run-usage.md:414:- It performs **no ledger backfill**: swept sessions are never written into the
docs/host-run-usage.md:416:- It is strictly **read-only**. The only write it can perform is an explicit
docs/host-run-usage.md:417:  `--out <path>` JSON report, and that write is create-only and fenced:
docs/host-run-usage.md:418:  - `--out` must be a **relative** path that resolves inside the project root;
docs/host-run-usage.md:419:    absolute paths and any `..` traversal escaping the root are refused
docs/host-run-usage.md:421:  - It only ever **creates a new report file** — the file is opened with the
docs/host-run-usage.md:422:    exclusive-create `wx` flag, so an already-existing target is refused
docs/host-run-usage.md:423:    atomically and `usage_sweep` can never overwrite or truncate anything
docs/host-run-usage.md:424:    (not even via a symlink at the target path).
docs/host-run-usage.md:425:  - It refuses to write through **symlinked ancestor directories**, and the
docs/host-run-usage.md:426:    resolved real path must still fall inside the (realpath'd) project root,
docs/host-run-usage.md:427:    so an inside-root symlink cannot redirect the report outside the project.
docs/host-run-usage.md:428:  - Missing report directories are created only **after** all of those checks
docs/host-run-usage.md:429:    pass.
docs/host-run-usage.md:430:  - Because `--out` writes a file into the material tree, a **non-empty `--out`
docs/host-run-usage.md:431:    is dynamically classified `storyScopedMutating`** by the ownership gate
docs/host-run-usage.md:432:    (F-014), so it is refused in read-only reviewer mode
docs/host-run-usage.md:433:    (`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1`) and on a retired root; without `--out`,
docs/host-run-usage.md:434:    `usage_sweep` stays read-only and runnable by any session.
docs/host-run-usage.md:435:  - The **same `--out` boundary governs the CLI activity / hook layer** (F-028):
docs/host-run-usage.md:436:    a plain (no-`--out`) `usage_sweep` is read-only there too, so it runs **no
docs/host-run-usage.md:437:    pre/post command hooks** and writes **no activity-log entry by default** (the
docs/host-run-usage.md:438:    `LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY=1` read-only heartbeat override documented
docs/host-run-usage.md:439:    in docs/CLI.md still applies); a non-empty `--out` is treated as a write and
docs/host-run-usage.md:440:    runs the hooks + records activity like any other mutating command.
docs/host-run-usage.md:441:  - The same boundary also governs the **codex process-event surface** (F-032):
docs/host-run-usage.md:442:    under `LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex` cli-engine appends a `codex_cli` event
docs/host-run-usage.md:443:    to the active story's `process-events.jsonl` after a command. That append is
docs/host-run-usage.md:444:    STORY metadata, so it obeys the identical read-only contract — a plain
docs/host-run-usage.md:445:    (no-`--out`) `usage_sweep` appends **no process event** (even with an
docs/host-run-usage.md:446:    inferred active story), while a non-empty `--out` (a write) records the
docs/host-run-usage.md:447:    process event like any other mutating command. The owner-lease heartbeat is
docs/host-run-usage.md:448:    intentionally exempt: it is keyed on the ownership class (only a
docs/host-run-usage.md:449:    `storyScopedMutating`/`dangerousMutating` write touches the lease), never on
docs/host-run-usage.md:450:    this read-only classification, so read-only session upkeep is unaffected.
docs/host-run-usage.md:454:- Usage rows **never gate the workflow** — they are `gateEvidence=false`
docs/host-run-usage.md:455:  diagnostics and are not consumed by any REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority gate.
docs/host-run-usage.md:456:- Interactive desktop host sessions are **out of reach** of the choke point;
docs/host-run-usage.md:457:  they are report-only via `usage_sweep`, never through `host_run`.
docs/host-run-usage.md:458:- `usage_sweep` never mutates story, ledger, or lifecycle state and never
docs/host-run-usage.md:459:  backfills the ledger.

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:377:#### M1 command-local syndrome preflight
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:379:Current-state proof consumers may reuse a command-local evidence hash snapshot
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:380:inside one CLI command invocation to avoid recomputing the same tuple across
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:381:DONE / review gate rows. The snapshot is exact hash-bound: `gitCwd`,
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:382:`metadataRoot`, `ref`, `headHash`, `materialHash`, `storyFilesHash`, capture
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:383:time, and material dirty files. Reuse is allowed only after a cheap syndrome
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:384:preflight confirms the same git cwd/ref/metadata root, the same current HEAD,
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:385:and no material dirty files. If the preflight fails, the consumer must capture a
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:386:fresh binding or report that the supplied snapshot is not reusable.

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:389:write evidence/runtime artifacts, and does not use mtime or file-count freshness

docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:737:## 9. Risk And Mitigation
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:739:| Risk after hardening | Why it can happen | Mitigation |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:741:| Old evidence becomes inadmissible | New contract requires fields old artifacts never had | Mark as `legacy-observed`; keep readable but not strong proof |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:742:| Old signatures fail | Canonical payload or strict shape changes | Add `schemaVersion` / `verifierVersion`; versioned verifiers |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:743:| False blocks increase | Gates reject evidence that was previously accepted | Start in warn mode; enforce only on high-risk policies |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:744:| User metadata gets stripped unexpectedly | Reserved key sanitizer deletes proof-looking keys | Strip only registered reserved keys; preserve ordinary metadata |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:745:| Handoff feels stricter | New host cannot treat worker output as DONE evidence | Show context/candidate/proof split in handoff preflight |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:746:| Implementation forks logic again | Each gate reimplements its own proof test | Require shared helper and process-fact registry verification |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:747:| Performance cost | Extra digest/signature/shape checks | Cache read-only classifications per gate evaluation; benchmark large stories |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:749:## 10. Verification Matrix
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:751:| Scenario | Expected result |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:753:| Caller preloads reserved proof key into metadata | Strip or reject; never admissible proof |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:754:| Direct job spoofs delegated metadata | Not classified as server-owned proof |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:755:| Edit gate-consumed `reason` field | Digest/signature mismatch or semantic binding failure |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:756:| Add `null` into signed bundle | Strict shape rejects before acceptance |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:757:| Add unexpected key into proof artifact | Strict shape rejects |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:758:| Use old material hash | `stale_material` |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:759:| Use wrong story id | `story_mismatch` |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:760:| Use wrong target phase | `gate_phase_mismatch` |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:761:| Use local/shadow `accepted=true` | `local-diagnostic`, not Authority proof |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:762:| Submit handoff diagnostic receipt | Accepted as diagnostic only; `productionDone=false` |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:763:| Read old evidence missing new fields | `legacy-observed`, audit-readable |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:764:| Valid new Authority `gate_decision` receipt consumed by matching adapter | `production-gate-decision`, admissible as evidence/input; local CLI core keeps `productionDone=false` |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:765:| Raw red probe without accepted ReproReview | `evidence-candidate` only; not a valid historical baseline |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:766:| Historical red uses old baseline hashes | `historical-valid`; not stale merely because current HEAD changed, but cannot independently satisfy a current-state gate |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:767:| Current green does not match current story hash tuple | stale current-state evidence |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:768:| Red and green command specs differ without equivalence review | `red_green_command_mismatch` |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:769:| Candidate artifact content changes after ReproReview | artifact digest mismatch |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:770:| Bootstrap failure matches no expected target pattern | `bootstrap_noise`; no repro-first claim |
docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md:771:| Regression matrix verdict is `matrix-gap` | REVIEW/TEST/DONE blocked unless explicit policy exception |

 ## Read-Only Reviewer Mode (`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1`)
 
 The command classes above describe ownership coordination between *owner sessions*. A separate
 concern is **advisory external reviewers**: external Claude/Codex/Gemini processes delegated
 to inspect artifacts and return structured findings as text — they are not Proofbound gate
 reviewers and must not write lifecycle evidence directly.
 
 `LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` is an opt-in guard for these advisory reviewer processes. It
 layers on top of the `CommandPolicy` / owner-lease architecture:
 
 - The guard runs **before** `enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate` and before preCommand hooks, so a
   readonly reviewer cannot acquire an owner lease, use `--takeover`, or trigger any hook
   side-effect that requires mutating access.
 - Only `ownershipClass === 'readOnly'` commands (e.g. `session_brief`, `story_get`,
   `checklist_get`, `finding_list`) proceed. All other classes fail closed.
-- This mode does **not** change how normal Proofbound gate reviewers (`lattice-review-*`) work.
-  Those reviewers operate without `LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` set and must be able to call
-  `review_pass_set`, `finding_add`, `delivery_check_set`, etc.
+- This mode does **not** change how normal Proofbound gate reviewers (`lattice-review-*`) work,
+  but their evidence authority depends on the invocation path. A registered host adapter can
+  issue a signed, exact native-review invocation attestation; that broker-attested native
+  reviewer may call `review_pass_set`, `finding_add`, or `delivery_check_set` directly. A
+  cross-provider reviewer launched through ManagedHostRun must instead submit its provider-owned
+  proposal and let `managed_review_evidence_import` write the pass/finding after the successful
+  terminal receipt is sealed. Raw provider CLI processes and unregistered adapters are
+  advisory-only and cannot directly author gate evidence.
 
 This section is the current active contract for reviewer read-only mode. Older
 reviewer-role background may describe the same separation concept, but must not
 override the `LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` env name or the command class rules
 documented here.
 
 ## Out of Scope
 
 This design does not solve:
 
-- cryptographic identity or unforgeable agent identity
+- general human/agent identity outside the registered host-adapter attestation and managed receipt boundaries
 - cross-clone distributed locking
-- reviewer identity attestation
+- distributed reviewer identity attestation across machines or clones
 - malicious local users editing JSON by hand
 - replacing git as source of truth
 
 Those require a stronger trust model and should be separate work.
 
 ## Acceptance Criteria
 
 1. Two sessions mutating the same story: second session is rejected with owner guidance.
 2. Two sessions working different stories in DEV: both proceed.
 3. Two DONE operations: serialized by main write lock; no partial-DONE race.
 4. Concurrent `gap_log` of the same issue: produces one canonical finding or duplicate-of link.
 5. Stale lease takeover: allowed only with explicit takeover and event record.
 6. Active lease takeover: rejected unless `forceTakeover` or human-approved.
 7. `session_brief` clearly tells non-owner sessions to wait or stay read-only.
 8. Existing read-only reviewer workflows still work.
 
 ## Rollout Plan
 
 1. Add this document and command classification table. — done.
 2. Implement story owner lease for story-scoped mutations. — done (B-c55d).

 ### M1 — Automatic cross-host review + disagreement surfacing (crypto-deferred)  [build · medium · the mechanism crux]
 Decision (2026-07-03): M1 is **crypto-deferred**. On the current single-machine, same-operator
 setup, tamper-proofing (signed verdicts / pinned keys) defends against a non-existent adversary —
 the value we can earn today is the **adversarial joint decision**, not a signature. So M1 builds the

    36	- `host_run_cancel`: idempotently request cancellation;
    37	- `host_run_worker`: private runtime continuation, dispatchable internally but
    38	  hidden from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
    39	- `managed_review_proposal_set`: compatibility-only provider callback for older
    40	  adapters, not the formal managed happy path;
    41	- `managed_review_evidence_import`: verdict-free exact-receipt importer.
    42	
    43	`cross_host_review` remains the policy/profile owner for paired host verdicts,
    44	but its Codex leaf executes inside ManagedHostRun and exposes the managed run
    45	and receipt in host-B provenance.
    46	
    47	## State and liveness contract
    48	
    49	The states are `submitted`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and
    50	`timed_out`. Exactly one terminal file wins by exclusive creation. Repeated
    51	status, cancel and resume operations are idempotent and never create a new run.
    52	
    53	Two clocks are deliberately distinct:
    54	
    55	- `workerHeartbeatAt` shows that the supervisor can still update its durable
    56	  snapshot;
    57	- `lastProviderProgressAt` changes only when observable provider stdout/stderr
    58	  arrives.
    59	
    60	Neither clock is a completion oracle. A provider may legitimately be silent,
    61	and a worker heartbeat does not prove provider progress. Expiry of a 30-second
    62	observation wait is non-terminal: it only wakes the caller and never authorizes
    63	a retry. The `host_run_status` call is also the run's next-touch reconciler,
    64	however, so during that call an already-requested cancellation or an expired
    65	absolute deadline can legitimately publish the corresponding `cancelled` or
    66	`timed_out` terminal state.
    67	
    68	Every run has a finite absolute deadline (30 minutes by default, bounded to 24
    69	hours). Deadline or cancellation reconciliation performs bounded TERM, KILL,
    70	reap and residual probing. Replacement is safe only when cleanup facts prove
    71	there is no residual process group. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity remains
    72	`replacementSafe=false`; it is not guessed away.
    73	
    74	## Persistence and process ownership
    75	
    76	Each run has a 0700 directory at
    77	`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
    78	primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
    79	DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
    80	bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
    81	capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
    82	Prompt, capability and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot inputs;
    83	the worker validates and deletes them before provider launch. Only root and
    84	runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.
    85	
    86	On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Codex receives the
    87	prompt through documented stdin (`codex exec ... -`) and Claude receives a 0600
    88	one-shot prompt file. The current agy print launcher accepts prompt text only in
    89	argv, so managed agy execution refuses before provider spawn until agy exposes a
    90	stdin or protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms likewise refuse
    91	before provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup is equivalent.
    92	
    93	## Shared provider admission
    94	
    95	Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
    96	of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
    97	token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
    98	Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
    99	not process admission.
   100	
   101	A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
   102	reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
   103	checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
   104	already been reclaimed and reassigned.
   105	
   106	Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
   107	admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
   108	review evidence.
   109	
   110	## Formal managed reviewer evidence
   111	
   112	Native-host reviewers retain the existing signed ReviewRun plus direct
   113	ReviewPass/Finding flow. A cross-provider CLI reviewer uses a two-phase flow:
   114	
   115	1. The controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
   116	2. `host_run --managedReview` derives the exact assembled prompt and seals
   117	   story, provider, lane, ReviewRun, head, material, story-files and prompt
   118	   bindings.
   119	3. The managed prompt requires the provider's final assistant result to be one
   120	   bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope with
   121	   pass-or-findings and truthful read evidence. It cannot write final
   122	   `review_pass_set`/`finding_add` evidence from inside the managed run. After a
   123	   successful provider exit, the owning adapter selects only Codex's terminal
   124	   `item.completed` `agent_message` or Claude's terminal `result`; tool logs,
   125	   arbitrary stdout and controller fields are never proposal inputs. The worker
   126	   validates the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple and atomically writes
   127	   the immutable proposal. Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized final
   128	   envelopes fail the managed run closed. The older descriptor-authorized
   129	   `managed_review_proposal_set` callback remains compatibility-only.
   130	4. Successful terminal creation seals spec, proposal, result and event-journal
   131	   digests plus cleanup facts.
   132	5. The controller calls `managed_review_evidence_import` with only the exact
   133	   runId and receiptId. It cannot provide or alter verdict bytes.
   134	6. The importer preserves provider reviewer/lane/ReviewRun/read provenance and
   135	   writes the existing signed ReviewPass/Finding shape.
   136	7. Import time and the REVIEW gate both call the shared Proof Admissibility
   137	   registry/intake/evaluator and revalidate the current terminal, proposal,
   138	   journal, prompt and material tuple.
   139	
   140	Raw CLI output outside the trusted final-result adapter lane, usage-ledger rows, time-window correlations, pre-terminal
   141	proposals, failed/cancelled/timed-out terminals and controller-authored verdicts
   142	cannot upgrade to managed reviewer evidence. Raw same-UID CLI calls, forged
   143	environment values, stale process groups, terminal/reaped runs and
   144	ambiguous/multiple active candidates cannot borrow the descriptor authority.
   145	
   146	The authority classifications remain disjoint. A native-host reviewer keeps the
   147	signed ReviewRun plus direct ReviewPass/Finding path only when a registered
   148	host-adapter broker signs the exact closeout invocation. Its Ed25519 attestation
   149	binds Story, agent/lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch,
   150	adapter/host identity and a one-shot nonce. Lattice stores the registered public
   151	key and nonce-consumption record, but exposes no issuer command and stores no
   152	broker private key. `dispatch`, `review_run_start`, inherited environment values
   153	and raw provider CLIs cannot mint this authority. The host adapter must inject
   154	the signed attestation over a dedicated descriptor for the exact CLI process;
   155	without that integration, native direct evidence is advisory-only and formal
   156	review must use the managed path.
   157	
   158	Process ancestry is secondary evidence. An unobservable process table, as in a
   159	brokered desktop sandbox, does not negate a valid broker signature. When a full
   160	ancestry is observable, any mixed distinct provider families (Claude→Codex or
   161	Codex→Claude) veto direct evidence even if the nearest ancestor matches. The
   162	one-shot local nonce ledger prevents replay but is not represented as protection
   163	against a same-UID/root attacker capable of replacing trusted configuration or
   164	instrumenting the broker.
   165	
   166	A cross-provider CLI reviewer requires a managed terminal receipt;
   167	cross-provider CLI output without that receipt is advisory-only. An explicit
   168	`degraded-single-host` fallback is local DONE assurance through host-verdict
   169	evidence, not direct or managed REVIEW evidence, and cannot borrow either
   170	reviewer authority path.
   171	
   172	## Operator guidance
   173	
   174	`lattice dispatch` prints two explicit execution modes. A native subagent uses
   175	its host lifecycle. A cross-provider CLI reviewer must use `host_run
   176	--managedReview`; raw `bash + codex/claude/agy` is advisory-only and cannot
   177	satisfy the managed evidence path.
   178	
   179	Poll the same run with `host_run_status --waitMs 30000`. Continue observing the
   180	same run across silent intervals. Cancel only on an explicit operator decision.
   181	Start a replacement only after an authoritative terminal and only when its
   182	cleanup proves replacement safety.
   183	
   184	## Retention and trust boundary
   185	
   186	`lattice doctor` reports worker liveness, provider-progress observability,
   187	deadline/cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. Explicit
   188	`doctor --repair` garbage-collects heavy terminal run directories only beyond
   189	90 days and first revalidates sealed spec, result, event-journal, proposal and
   190	evidence-binding digests, then preserves the minimal receipt plus evidence-binding
   191	digest under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. Any mismatch is reported as
   192	corrupt and retained for manual review. Active or corrupt runs and
   193	runs that still contain one-shot inputs are retained fail-closed. Failed startup
   194	removes one-shot secrets immediately.
   195	
   196	The local filesystem boundary does not defend against a same-UID or root
   197	attacker. Retained output may contain sensitive provider text and must be
   198	treated accordingly.
   199	
   200	## Compatibility and non-goals
   201	
   202	- Existing finite provider timeouts, cross-host policy ceilings, bounded retry
   203	  and fail-closed classifications remain in force.
   204	- Ordinary non-review host runs remain compatible but now gain durable
   205	  ownership and shared admission.
   206	- No remote scheduler, daemon, queue or native-host subagent abstraction is
   207	  introduced.
   208	- Usage diagnostics remain non-authoritative and never become lifecycle proof.

     2	
     3	Status: Adopted
     4	Story: B-137a
     5	Date: 2026-08-14
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	When a Claude host started Codex (or a Codex host started Claude) with raw shell
    10	execution, the caller owned the child process implicitly. A caller watchdog,
    11	terminal disconnect, or ten-minute foreground boundary could end observation
    12	without proving that the provider had failed. Treating that loss of observation
    13	as failure caused duplicate reviewer launches; treating `running` forever as
    14	proof of health caused unbounded waits. Output silence alone answers neither
    15	question.
    16	
    17	Proofbound is host-neutral. Native Codex/Claude subagent lifecycle APIs are not
    18	portable and therefore are not the execution contract. This decision covers
    19	only Proofbound-owned cross-provider CLI processes.
    20	
    21	## Decision
    22	
    23	Proofbound owns every public `host_run` and every formal cross-provider CLI
    24	reviewer launch through a durable `ManagedHostRun`. General provider workloads
    25	such as planned steps and autopilot repair keep their existing bounded adapters
    26	but share the mandatory provider-process admission registry; they do not claim
    27	durable reviewer ownership or reviewer evidence. The caller submits and
    28	observes; a detached worker owns the managed provider process until an exclusive
    29	terminal record exists.
    30	
    31	The public surface is:
    32	
    33	- `host_run`: submit, optionally attach in foreground, or return after claim
    34	  with `--detach`;
    35	- `host_run_status`: read or long-poll one run for at most 30 seconds;
    36	- `host_run_cancel`: idempotently request cancellation;
    37	- `host_run_worker`: private runtime continuation, dispatchable internally but
    38	  hidden from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
    39	- `managed_review_proposal_set`: compatibility-only provider callback for older
    40	  adapters, not the formal managed happy path;
    41	- `managed_review_evidence_import`: verdict-free exact-receipt importer.
    42	
    43	`cross_host_review` remains the policy/profile owner for paired host verdicts,
    44	but its Codex leaf executes inside ManagedHostRun and exposes the managed run
    45	and receipt in host-B provenance.
    46	
    47	## State and liveness contract
    48	
    49	The states are `submitted`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and
    50	`timed_out`. Exactly one terminal file wins by exclusive creation. Repeated
    51	status, cancel and resume operations are idempotent and never create a new run.
    52	
    53	Two clocks are deliberately distinct:
    54	
    55	- `workerHeartbeatAt` shows that the supervisor can still update its durable
    56	  snapshot;
    57	- `lastProviderProgressAt` changes only when observable provider stdout/stderr
    58	  arrives.
    59	
    60	Neither clock is a completion oracle. A provider may legitimately be silent,
    61	and a worker heartbeat does not prove provider progress. Expiry of a 30-second
    62	observation wait is non-terminal: it only wakes the caller and never authorizes
    63	a retry. The `host_run_status` call is also the run's next-touch reconciler,
    64	however, so during that call an already-requested cancellation or an expired
    65	absolute deadline can legitimately publish the corresponding `cancelled` or
    66	`timed_out` terminal state.
    67	
    68	Every run has a finite absolute deadline (30 minutes by default, bounded to 24
    69	hours). Deadline or cancellation reconciliation performs bounded TERM, KILL,
    70	reap and residual probing. Replacement is safe only when cleanup facts prove
    71	there is no residual process group. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity remains
    72	`replacementSafe=false`; it is not guessed away.
    73	
    74	## Persistence and process ownership
    75	
    76	Each run has a 0700 directory at
    77	`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
    78	primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
    79	DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
    80	bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
    81	capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
    82	Prompt, capability and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot inputs;
    83	the worker validates and deletes them before provider launch. Only root and
    84	runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.
    85	
    86	On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Codex receives the
    87	prompt through documented stdin (`codex exec ... -`) and Claude receives a 0600
    88	one-shot prompt file. The current agy print launcher accepts prompt text only in
    89	argv, so managed agy execution refuses before provider spawn until agy exposes a
    90	stdin or protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms likewise refuse
    91	before provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup is equivalent.
    92	
    93	## Shared provider admission
    94	
    95	Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
    96	of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
    97	token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
    98	Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
    99	not process admission.
   100	
   101	A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
   102	reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
   103	checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
   104	already been reclaimed and reassigned.
   105	
   106	Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
   107	admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
   108	review evidence.
   109	
   110	## Formal managed reviewer evidence
   111	
   112	Native-host reviewers retain the existing signed ReviewRun plus direct
   113	ReviewPass/Finding flow. A cross-provider CLI reviewer uses a two-phase flow:
   114	
   115	1. The controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
   116	2. `host_run --managedReview` derives the exact assembled prompt and seals
   117	   story, provider, lane, ReviewRun, head, material, story-files and prompt
   118	   bindings.
   119	3. The managed prompt requires the provider's final assistant result to be one
   120	   bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope with
   121	   pass-or-findings and truthful read evidence. It cannot write final
   122	   `review_pass_set`/`finding_add` evidence from inside the managed run. After a
   123	   successful provider exit, the owning adapter selects only Codex's terminal
   124	   `item.completed` `agent_message` or Claude's terminal `result`; tool logs,
   125	   arbitrary stdout and controller fields are never proposal inputs. The worker
   126	   validates the exact story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple and atomically writes
   127	   the immutable proposal. Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized final
   128	   envelopes fail the managed run closed. The older descriptor-authorized
   129	   `managed_review_proposal_set` callback remains compatibility-only.
   130	4. Successful terminal creation seals spec, proposal, result and event-journal
   131	   digests plus cleanup facts.
   132	5. The controller calls `managed_review_evidence_import` with only the exact
   133	   runId and receiptId. It cannot provide or alter verdict bytes.
   134	6. The importer preserves provider reviewer/lane/ReviewRun/read provenance and
   135	   writes the existing signed ReviewPass/Finding shape.
   136	7. Import time and the REVIEW gate both call the shared Proof Admissibility
   137	   registry/intake/evaluator and revalidate the current terminal, proposal,
   138	   journal, prompt and material tuple.
   139	
   140	Raw CLI output outside the trusted final-result adapter lane, usage-ledger rows, time-window correlations, pre-terminal
   141	proposals, failed/cancelled/timed-out terminals and controller-authored verdicts
   142	cannot upgrade to managed reviewer evidence. Raw same-UID CLI calls, forged
   143	environment values, stale process groups, terminal/reaped runs and
   144	ambiguous/multiple active candidates cannot borrow the descriptor authority.
   145	
   146	The authority classifications remain disjoint. A native-host reviewer keeps the
   147	signed ReviewRun plus direct ReviewPass/Finding path only when a registered
   148	host-adapter broker signs the exact closeout invocation. Its Ed25519 attestation
   149	binds Story, agent/lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch,
   150	adapter/host identity and a one-shot nonce. Lattice stores the registered public
   151	key and nonce-consumption record, but exposes no issuer command and stores no
   152	broker private key. `dispatch`, `review_run_start`, inherited environment values
   153	and raw provider CLIs cannot mint this authority. The host adapter must inject
   154	the signed attestation over a dedicated descriptor for the exact CLI process;
   155	without that integration, native direct evidence is advisory-only and formal
   156	review must use the managed path.
   157	
   158	Process ancestry is secondary evidence. An unobservable process table, as in a
   159	brokered desktop sandbox, does not negate a valid broker signature. When a full
   160	ancestry is observable, any mixed distinct provider families (Claude→Codex or
   161	Codex→Claude) veto direct evidence even if the nearest ancestor matches. The
   162	one-shot local nonce ledger prevents replay but is not represented as protection
   163	against a same-UID/root attacker capable of replacing trusted configuration or
   164	instrumenting the broker.
   165	
   166	A cross-provider CLI reviewer requires a managed terminal receipt;
   167	cross-provider CLI output without that receipt is advisory-only. An explicit
   168	`degraded-single-host` fallback is local DONE assurance through host-verdict
   169	evidence, not direct or managed REVIEW evidence, and cannot borrow either
   170	reviewer authority path.
   171	
   172	## Operator guidance
   173	
   174	`lattice dispatch` prints two explicit execution modes. A native subagent uses
   175	its host lifecycle. A cross-provider CLI reviewer must use `host_run
   176	--managedReview`; raw `bash + codex/claude/agy` is advisory-only and cannot
   177	satisfy the managed evidence path.
   178	
   179	Poll the same run with `host_run_status --waitMs 30000`. Continue observing the
   180	same run across silent intervals. Cancel only on an explicit operator decision.
   181	Start a replacement only after an authoritative terminal and only when its
   182	cleanup proves replacement safety.
   183	
   184	## Retention and trust boundary
   185	
   186	`lattice doctor` reports worker liveness, provider-progress observability,
   187	deadline/cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. Explicit
   188	`doctor --repair` garbage-collects heavy terminal run directories only beyond
   189	90 days and first revalidates sealed spec, result, event-journal, proposal and
   190	evidence-binding digests, then preserves the minimal receipt plus evidence-binding
   191	digest under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. Any mismatch is reported as
   192	corrupt and retained for manual review. Active or corrupt runs and
   193	runs that still contain one-shot inputs are retained fail-closed. Failed startup
   194	removes one-shot secrets immediately.
   195	
   196	The local filesystem boundary does not defend against a same-UID or root
   197	attacker. Retained output may contain sensitive provider text and must be
   198	treated accordingly.
   199	
   200	## Compatibility and non-goals
   201	
   202	- Existing finite provider timeouts, cross-host policy ceilings, bounded retry
   203	  and fail-closed classifications remain in force.
   204	- Ordinary non-review host runs remain compatible but now gain durable
   205	  ownership and shared admission.
   206	- No remote scheduler, daemon, queue or native-host subagent abstraction is
   207	  introduced.
   208	- Usage diagnostics remain non-authoritative and never become lifecycle proof.

 ## Idempotency Requirements
 
 Inside the relevant lock:
 
 - `story_create` deduplicates by normalized name and keyword overlap.
 - `gap_log` deduplicates by normalized title, category, source, and evidence fingerprint.
 - finding mutations reject duplicate active findings unless explicitly linked as `duplicate-of`.
 - DONE recovery detects already-merged branches and already-removed worktrees.
 
 ## Read-Only Reviewer Mode (`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1`)
 
 The command classes above describe ownership coordination between *owner sessions*. A separate
 concern is **advisory external reviewers**: external Claude/Codex/Gemini processes delegated
 to inspect artifacts and return structured findings as text — they are not Proofbound gate
 reviewers and must not write lifecycle evidence directly.
 
 `LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` is an opt-in guard for these advisory reviewer processes. It
 layers on top of the `CommandPolicy` / owner-lease architecture:
 
 - The guard runs **before** `enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate` and before preCommand hooks, so a
   readonly reviewer cannot acquire an owner lease, use `--takeover`, or trigger any hook
   side-effect that requires mutating access.
 - Only `ownershipClass === 'readOnly'` commands (e.g. `session_brief`, `story_get`,
   `checklist_get`, `finding_list`) proceed. All other classes fail closed.
-- This mode does **not** change how normal Proofbound gate reviewers (`lattice-review-*`) work.
-  Those reviewers operate without `LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` set and must be able to call
-  `review_pass_set`, `finding_add`, `delivery_check_set`, etc.
+- This mode does **not** change how normal Proofbound gate reviewers (`lattice-review-*`) work,
+  but their evidence authority depends on the invocation path. A registered host adapter can
+  issue a signed, exact native-review invocation attestation; that broker-attested native
+  reviewer may call `review_pass_set`, `finding_add`, or `delivery_check_set` directly. A
+  cross-provider reviewer launched through ManagedHostRun must instead submit its provider-owned
+  proposal and let `managed_review_evidence_import` write the pass/finding after the successful
+  terminal receipt is sealed. Raw provider CLI processes and unregistered adapters are
+  advisory-only and cannot directly author gate evidence.
 
 This section is the current active contract for reviewer read-only mode. Older
 reviewer-role background may describe the same separation concept, but must not
 override the `LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1` env name or the command class rules
 documented here.
 
 ## Out of Scope
 
 This design does not solve:
 
-- cryptographic identity or unforgeable agent identity
+- general human/agent identity outside the registered host-adapter attestation and managed receipt boundaries
 - cross-clone distributed locking
-- reviewer identity attestation
+- distributed reviewer identity attestation across machines or clones
 - malicious local users editing JSON by hand
 - replacing git as source of truth
 
 Those require a stronger trust model and should be separate work.

 1. Two sessions mutating the same story: second session is rejected with owner guidance.
 2. Two sessions working different stories in DEV: both proceed.

 5. Stale lease takeover: allowed only with explicit takeover and event record.
 6. Active lease takeover: rejected unless `forceTakeover` or human-approved.

 8. Existing read-only reviewer workflows still work.

 Today all evidence (Tier-A engine contract, Tier-B powered ablation) is produced on one operator's
 machine — a skeptic must trust the operator. Tier-C makes two **independent vendor hosts**
 (Claude + Codex) each emit a **cryptographically signed** verdict on the same code, such that any
 third party can **offline-verify** both signatures and their binding to that exact code. It moves
 trust from "trust the operator" to "trust the math + two independent vendors." This is the strongest
 form of the thesis and the sole gap the paper names for Tier-C.
 
 ## 2. Milestones
 
 Cheap proof-of-mechanism = M0–M3 (days each, ~zero research risk). Expensive strong claim = M4

3-## Problem
4:When reviewer lanes run in parallel, or a reviewer retries review_run_start, a second run_start on the same (storyId, lane) in the same reviewRound mints a newer reviewRunId. currentRunForLane (review-run.ts) returns the newest-by-recency run, and any review_pass_set / finding_add bound to the ORIGINAL run is hard-rejected — at write time by assertCurrentReviewRunForEvidence (review-run.ts:669-672, "is not the current latest reviewer run") and at validate time by validateEvidenceRunBinding (review-run.ts:794-804, issue 'stale_run') — purely because a newer run exists, even though the bound run is still in the current round and still material- and scope-fresh. This empties the lane's valid-pass set and stalls quorum_submit (handlers/quorum-submit.ts), which forced a whole fresh REVIEW round during B-70e4. reviewerWrite is lease-exempt (command-policy.ts) and review_run_start vs review_pass_set/finding_add hold DISTINCT mkdir locks, so the owner lease never serialized these writers; B-77ed only raised the lock budget to 30s, which does not address the false-reject.
5-
6-## Decision
7:Remove the id-recency rejection: a non-latest run is ACCEPTED when it is still material-fresh and scope-fresh, and rejected only by the existing freshness and scope checks (stale-by-material/scope, never stale-merely-by-id). The validate-side relax is KIND-AWARE: the 'stale_run' issue is dropped only for evidence.kind === 'pass' (so a material-fresh non-latest PASS becomes valid), but KEPT for findings so an older OPEN finding is still surfaced and not hidden by a newer pass on the same lane (collectReviewerEvidenceState supersedes it only once the finding is resolved/dismissed). This is conditioned on a mandatory soundness guard added to checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit: the storyFilesHash drift-advisory downgrade must treat EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH (sha256 of an empty story-owned diff) as no-signal on BOTH the stored and the live side and fall through to strict materialHash, exactly as delivery-check-hash.ts:184-188 already does. The lease-contract doc (session-ownership-and-write-leases.md) is reconciled doc-only.
8-
9-## Why id-recency is redundant
10:Both surviving checks compare the run's CAPTURED SNAPSHOT against the LIVE current state, never run-1 against run-2: checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit reads currentMaterialHash / currentStoryFilesHash from live HEAD; compareScopeBinding re-digests the live contract and the live main...HEAD diff pack. A second run_start changes only the reviewRunId, not what was reviewed; two same-round runs that captured the same tree are byte-identical to the live comparison. Round, lane, signature (verifyReviewRun), and workspace-binding checks all still fire.
11-
12-## The one real hole and its guard
13-The adversarial soundness review found that the storyFilesHash drift-advisory branch — the sole path where whole-tree material drift does not hard-reject — lacked the EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH no-signal guard. currentStoryFilesHash returns a truthy sha256('') for an empty story diff; under relax, a same-round run captured with an empty story diff could ride the advisory under arbitrary whole-tree drift while a newer run captured the real current state. The mandatory EMPTY guard closes this for all checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit callers.
14-
15-## Rejected alternatives
16-- keep-strict: preserves the quorum-blocking false-reject for a check that adds no soundness.
17-- unify-lock-A alone: does NOT fix the race — a legitimate later run_start still invalidates an earlier fresh pass under strict id-recency; it only narrows the interleave window. Deferred as an optional follow-up.
18-- blanket relax (both kinds) without the EMPTY guard and without kind-awareness: unsound under empty-set storyFilesHash drift, AND it hides open findings behind a newer pass. Both were caught by a red->spike->story spike plus the adversarial design review, which is why the validate-side relax is kind-aware and the EMPTY guard is mandatory.
19-
20-## Scope
21:Both review-run.ts call sites (assertCurrentReviewRunForEvidence write-time and validateEvidenceRunBinding validate-time); the EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH guard in checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit (evidence-freshness.ts, all callers); and the lease-doc reconciliation.
